The measure stood at 0.6 percentage points against a 0.75-point trigger after unemployment reached 4.9% in October. Independent economist Saul Eslake said it could cross the threshold in December if the recent pace of increase continued, with confirmation coming in data due January 21.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers told Parliament in Canberra that the government expects unemployment to exceed 5% and growth to slow below 2%, while neither Treasury nor the Reserve Bank of Australia forecasts an economic contraction. The rule tracks how quickly unemployment rises, which former U.S. Federal Reserve economist Claudia Sahm said can signal mounting strain for workers before standard recession measures confirm a downturn.

title: Anthropic mathematician says Claude outpaced him near proof's finish
description:
Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says the company’s Claude AI took a larger role as they worked on a claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a famous problem about prime numbers. Alpöge said he guided the effort by combining two mathematical ideas, but Claude moved faster than he did near the end. Separate Lean and Mathlib groups have since verified the formalized proof.

The collaboration lasted about six weeks, from early October to Nov. 16, according to Alpöge’s account. He has not yet published a readable mathematical explanation, leaving researchers to work out the argument behind the computer-checked result.

The announcement came a day after Anthropic’s stock-market debut, prompting questions about its timing. Alpöge called the timing “horrible” and said he would have finished earlier if he could. He denied that the release was coordinated with the listing.

title: AI buyers broaden chip choices as Nvidia faces leadership uncertainty
description:
AI companies are exploring alternatives to Nvidia following the Nov. 12 departure of its co-founder and chief executive, Jensen Huang. AI company Anthropic is spreading its infrastructure across suppliers, while rivals AMD and Google are building competing systems. Nvidia’s interim chief executive, Colette Kress, said demand remained strong on the company’s latest earnings call.

AMD is pitching its Helios rack-scale platform, while Google has expanded its Tensor Processing Unit offerings. Nvidia’s CUDA software ecosystem remains a switching hurdle for customers whose applications and teams rely on it. Anthropic uses accelerators from Nvidia, AMD and Google, though its sourcing strategy alone does not establish their relative performance or costs.

title: Libya seeks UN probe after suspected drone strikes hit Benghazi ships
description:
The United Nations Support Mission in Libya called Monday for an immediate, independent investigation after two ships were attacked near Benghazi, urging restraint and respect for Libyan sovereignty. Satellite imagery identified the Russian Navy corvette Merkury as the ship hit inside the port on Sunday. It capsized and sank, and 10 people, including Russians and Libyans, suffered minor injuries. A Malta-flagged commercial vessel was struck offshore later, and its crew was rescued. Libyan forces intercepted more than 20 drone boats, Libyan military sources told Reuters.

The eastern Libyan administration said preliminary findings pointed to a drone attack on the Russian ship, which had stopped to refuel and take on supplies while returning to Russia under maritime cooperation agreements. It ordered a joint investigation with Moscow, requested an international inquiry through the United Nations and sought formal explanations from Ukraine about its military activity in Libya.

Libya’s rival, internationally recognized Government of National Unity in Tripoli warned that using ports and civilian facilities for conflicts abroad threatens Libyan security and state assets. The U.N. mission urged parties not to circulate unverified claims or politicize the investigation and said it was ready to assist Libyan authorities.

title: Google finds hackers using AI to run autonomous cyberattacks
description:
Google’s threat researchers say they found a cyberattack system that used artificial intelligence to identify software flaws, create exploits and carry out intrusions with little or no human direction. The system, called exploit_agent, ran on an exposed server and linked several language models. Scripts also mapped networks, guessed passwords and installed webshells. Google said the activity marks a shift from AI-assisted hacking to automated attacks.

Attackers are using open-source AI penetration-testing frameworks against real targets. Google reported that attackers exploited two PaperCut print-server flaws in August, with one campaign reaching hundreds of organizations four days after disclosure. Amazon separately documented an AI-assisted intrusion using Cairn that targeted East Asian educational institutions in September. The U.S. Government Accountability Office said AI reduces the human effort needed for complex attacks and cited a fully autonomous ransomware operation.

Google says these systems currently sacrifice stealth for speed but expects attacks to become harder to detect. Microsoft President Brad Smith warned that faster vulnerability discovery is forcing companies to patch more quickly, while rushed updates can disrupt older systems.

title: Webb and gravitational waves reveal clues to black hole origins
description:
A James Webb Space Telescope study identified a possible black hole in the young galaxy MARTA 3887, seen as it was about 12 billion years ago. Its estimated mass is 3.3 million suns—about 2.3% of the galaxy’s stellar mass. Separately, researchers analyzing 257 black-hole mergers found a concentration near 10 solar masses and a shortage between 12 and 16, a pattern consistent with some massive stars collapsing without supernova explosions.

The Webb team says a supernova or gas outflow could mimic the black-hole signal, and its evidence comes from a single observation. The merger study does not directly confirm failed supernovae; researchers say more work is needed to test that explanation.

Detection limits: Astronomical surveys may disproportionately detect the brightest black holes or those with the fastest-moving gas, while signals from supernovae, shocks and outflows can make smaller, more typical black holes difficult to distinguish (phys.org). title: German rocket maker starts building Nova Scotia launch complex for 2028
description:
German rocket maker Isar Aerospace took control of its designated site at Spaceport Nova Scotia on Nov. 21 and began building a launch complex for its Spectrum rocket. The facility near Canso will include a final assembly line and a satellite payload preparation site.

The complex is Isar’s second launch location and its first in North America. The company and spaceport developer Maritime Launch Services are targeting initial orbital launches in 2028.

title: Dutch court blocks BYD SUV sales in EU over Defender design
description:
The District Court of The Hague has temporarily barred Chinese automaker BYD from selling its seven-seat Ti7 SUV in the European Union, ruling that its design infringes Jaguar Land Rover’s (JLR) EU design rights for the Defender. The order also halts production of the SUV at BYD’s new plant in Hungary while the case proceeds. The injunction takes effect one week after Friday’s ruling. The court said BYD had no concrete plans to launch the Ti7 in the EU. It also said it lacked jurisdiction over BYD’s UK business, where deliveries are scheduled to begin in January 2027.

BYD says it will appeal and maintains that the Ti7 was independently designed, while JLR says it takes legal action to protect its intellectual property. A final decision on the infringement claim is expected next year. BYD had planned to bring the model to Europe as it expands overseas to offset pressure on profits in China.

It also said it lacked jurisdiction over BYD’s UK business, where deliveries are scheduled to begin in January 2027 (theguardian.com, dr.dk). BYD says it will appeal and maintains that the Ti7 was independently designed, while JLR says it takes legal action to protect its intellectual property (ft.com, theguardian.com). A final decision on the infringement claim is expected next year (ft.com). BYD had planned to bring the model to Europe as it expands overseas to offset pressure on profits in China (ft.com). Design findings: The Dutch court cited the Ti7’s characteristic and distinctive design elements; reported similarities include its boxy body, flat roof, squared wheel arches and tailgate (vnexpress.net, scmp.com). UK price: BYD lists the Ti7 in the UK for £47,995, more than £20,000 below a comparable Defender (theguardian.com).

title: 'COP31 Was a Colossal Failure': Longest UN Climate Summit Collapses Without Deal
description:
The longest United Nations Climate Change Conference on record ended in overtime on Sunday, with the governments gathered in Türkiye for COP31 unable to reach an agreement on tackling the fossil fuel-driven global emergency.

The Turkish and Australian governments hosted the conference in Antalya. According to The Guardian, Australia's minister for climate change and energy, Chris Bowen, told reporters outside the plenary room that he hadn't slept for three days.

"Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision, and that's very disappointing," Bowen said, hours after the latest draft drew a fresh wave of criticism. "Ultimately, looking back, many parties who are people of good faith had very strong red lines on a couple of key issues, and despite many, many attempts, on reflection those red lines were not able to be met."

The European Union, Panama, and small island nations were among those that rejected the proposal. Explaining the EU's position, the Irish climate and environment minister, Darragh O'Brien, said that "it is unconscionable that we would have a climate act that makes no reference to fossil fuel, no reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels."

While Big Oil-backed US President Donald Trump has ditched the Paris Agreement and declined to send a delegation to COP31, even though his country is the largest historical climate polluter, other major petroleum producers such as Saudi Arabia and Russia lobbied against mentioning fossil fuels. Panama's climate minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, told Politico that "the world is hostage to petroleum producers. That is the truth... And they will not stop."

In the lead-up to the conference, scientists warned that temporarily surpassing the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C threshold for temperature rise this century, relative to preindustrial levels, is now inevitable, and the world is barreling toward "an irrecoverable overshoot" of that target absent a rapid reduction in planet-heating emissions.

Jasper Inventor, head of the Greenpeace International delegation at COP31, said that "it's bitterly disappointing to leave without a clear outcome or a credible pathway to end fossil fuels. We stopped a bad deal that favors fossil fuels, but leaving without a deal is still a failure for communities on the climate frontlines. As always, it is the world's most vulnerable communities who bear the consequences of this failure. We've run out of time to avoid overshoot, but we can still keep 1.5°C alive."

Climate campaigners from around the world joined Inventor in expressing frustration that "COP31 has failed to deliver any meaningful outcomes on climate action," as Oxfam International climate change policy lead Nafkote Dabi put it after two weeks of talks. "Shame on rich polluting countries for once again turning their backs on communities fighting for survival in a climate crisis they did little to cause. Shame on the presidencies for prioritizing profits and ego over progress."

"And shame on all the countries that stubbornly blocked and distracted from discussions meant to deliver crucial funding to people watching their homes swallowed by floods, their crops wither in droughts, and their lives upended by deadly heat," said Dabi. "Instead of implementation, COP31 has delivered yet another victory for rich polluting countries and fossil fuel interests. The co-presidencies—who both remain heavily invested in fossil fuels and are profiting from climate destruction—attempted to broker a decision without a single mention of fossil fuels in favor of false solutions."

View on X

Nikki Reisch, a director at the Center for International Environmental Law, explained that "the proposed cover decision did not advance the provision of climate finance, said nothing about the root cause of the crisis, and made no mention of states' legal obligations to prevent and repair climate harm, as clarified by the International Court of Justice. On loss and damage, it fared no better as it offered little more than expressions of deep concern about mounting impacts. And a text that welcomed a scale-up of future fantasy fixes like carbon dioxide removal (CDR) technologies and proven-to-fail industry favorites like carbon capture and storage (CCS), without so much as a whisper about fossil fuels, would have been a massive giveaway to polluters."

Calling out the hosts, Global Climate and Health Alliance executive director Jeni Miller stressed that "the rightly rejected 'Antalya Pact' comes as climate change compounds this year's super El Niño, causing severe droughts in Fiji and Bolivia, extreme flooding in the western US, and wildfires in Southeast Asia, and putting millions of additional people at risk of hunger or famine."

Amiera Sawas, head of research and policy at the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative, highlighted that "while Global North countries rejected the outcome on the basis that there was no language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, these same countries have not themselves presented serious or credible phaseout plans, nor do they intend to support others in their transitions. Many wealthy countries continue expanding fossil fuel extraction despite their international legal obligations, while developing countries carrying unpayable debt can't plan an exit at all."

"The EU and some of its most powerful member states have blocked progress or, worse, reneged on past commitments," Sawas continued. "Demanding the words 'fossil fuels' in the cover text while blocking mandated agenda items and pointing fingers at developing countries is acting in bad faith. We need real commitments to a fair and financed phaseout of fossil fuels that delivers on the Paris Agreement, not collapses it. That means a just transition, where those most responsible pay their fair share and workers, communities, and Indigenous peoples have a meaningful say in what it looks like."

View on X

Mohamed Adow, director of the think tank Power Shift Africa, declared that "this has been the worst ever COP, and its collapse needs to be a wake-up call for the world. Rich nations and polluting governments cannot keep arriving empty-handed and expecting a carefully worded declaration to get them off the hook."

Romain Ioualalen, global policy lead at Oil Change International, similarly asserted that "this will go down as one of the worst COPs in history. COP hosts Australia and Türkiye have failed to steward the negotiations. This sad stalemate only benefits fossil fuel interests while people and communities will continue paying the highest price for the crisis they didn't create."

"Don't fall for the EU's attempt to portray themselves as heroes. They are the ones who are largely to blame for this result... But let's be clear: The outcome on the table was dangerous," he continued, welcoming the proposal's defeat. "Countries failed to rise to the moment, but we refuse to lower the bar. The countries and communities fighting for climate justice are not backing down, and the road to COP32 in Ethiopia must be about action."

Asad Rehman, chief executive of Friends of the Earth in England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, also emphasized how bad the final deal was: "After decades of broken pledges and hollow commitments, an agreement built on yet more empty promises would have been unforgivable and no substitute for the transformative action we urgently need. So the dramatic rejection of the presidency's final text by some, though underscoring the lack of consensus that's been reached, restores some level of faith in its recognition that a deal of this caliber is no deal at all."

"What matters now is not when governments reconvene, it's how they do so," he argued. "The world doesn't need more meetings with woolly commitments. We need global governments, including the UK, to come back to the negotiating table ready to deliver. That means cutting emissions fairly at home, transitioning our economies in a way that leaves no one behind, and providing the public climate finance so desperately needed to protect people, livelihoods, and our planet from unimaginable harm."

View on X

Savio Carvalho, head of campaigns and networks at 350.org, also looked ahead: "You'd think that in the middle of the worst fossil fuel crisis in history, after a year of devastating wildfires, floods, and collapsing glaciers, world leaders would finally rise to the moment. But they didn't. We averted a truly bad outcome because many countries stood up to the fossil fuel industry and rejected dangerous distractions. But we still left COP31 without a clear plan to exit coal, oil, and gas. There's no real money on the table to help countries survive the climate breakdown that is already at our doorstep."

"The world needs governments with the courage to stand with people and the planet, even when the fossil fuel industry pushes back," Carvalho added. "This isn't the end. We'll keep pushing until governments end the age of fossil fuels. Every meeting and every decision in the year ahead counts. The time for delay is over."

The Turkish and Australian governments hosted the conference in Antalya.

title: Still Alive revived
description:
Still Alive revived

Back in 2008, I blogged about a little homebrew game for the Nintendo DS named StillAliveDS and how much I liked the puzzle platformer.

StillAliveDS is a puzzle game inspired by Portal: The Flash Version, which is a 2D remake of Portal, developed by Valve Corporation.

Portal consists primarily of a series of puzzles that must be solved by teleporting the character and other simple objects using a Portal Gun. The unusual physics allowed by the Portal Gun are the emphasis of Portal.

A few weeks ago, I used my website's random button and landed on exactly that post. I wondered whatever became of the game. To my surprise, I learned that its developer, “t4ils,” had made a web version and released it under the AGPL.

Unfortunately, the website was no longer available, but the Wayback Machine still had parts of it. There was enough to recover all the client-side code.

It still worked in modern browsers, but it used an ancient version of jQuery, and the tiny DS-resolution graphics weren't great on modern systems.

So I spent quite some time “reviving” the game with the help of Claude. I wanted to keep the gameplay, look, and feel as close to the original as possible while thoroughly modernizing the game.

To nobody's surprise, Claude was able to make the game run again in no time. Refactoring the code and graphics into a modern architecture, on the other hand, took a lot of babysitting and reviewing. The current architecture is the result of many, many iterations.

Tiles and background graphics had to be redrawn from scratch while staying close to the original. Though I made the creative decision to drop a few “jokes” from the background images that I felt were a bit out of date – I don't think anyone misses jokes about Michael Jackson's looks in 2026.

Since the licensing of the original audio was a bit unclear, I decided to replace the sound effects and also extend them to cover more actions. Finding the right effects took quite a while – Claude helped me by building a “sound lab” where I could test and compare sound effects from different free sources until I found what I needed.

Even though the game now uses a modern ES module structure and web components for the UI, I decided not to use a bundler. Instead, it relies on modern browsers' module-loading support. A custom loader loads all assets into RAM once. This way, there are no external dependencies (neither libraries nor build tools), and the game can be restored from the Wayback Machine, just like the original could.

The game can be played right in your browser: Still Alive revived.

Currently, only mouse and keyboard are supported. If I feel like it, I might add controller support someday. I don't know if or how it could ever be made to support touch controls.

title: CachyOS adds signed kernel for Easy Anti-Cheat Linux v2
description:
CachyOS, an Arch-based Linux distribution, released its November 2026 update with support for Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) Linux v2 through a dedicated signed kernel and boot entry for games that require it. The anti-cheat setup requires Secure Boot, a trusted signing key, TPM 2.0, an enabled IOMMU and kernel lockdown; CachyOS says users can keep their normal boot option alongside the EAC kernel. The release prepares systems for the anti-cheat but does not guarantee that any particular game will work with it; GamingOnLinux’s editor said he knew of no supported games at the time of publication.

The update also introduces CachyOS Package Installer 2.0, with optional AUR, Flatpak and AppImage support, and cachyos-recovery, a recovery environment that can restore Btrfs snapshots without external recovery media. The installation image includes Linux kernel 7.3.5, and the project also provides a Windows Subsystem for Linux image. Existing users switching to the new graphics-driver startup system must reinstall their driver profiles after updating, using the commands CachyOS recommends.

excerpt: CachyOS, an Arch-based Linux distribution, released its November 2026 update with support for Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) Linux v2 through a dedicated signed kernel and boot entry for games that require it (linuxiac.com, phoronix.com, gamingonlinux.com). The anti-cheat setup requires Secure Boot, a trusted signing key, TPM 2.0, an enabled IOMMU and kernel lockdown; CachyOS says users can keep their normal boot option alongside the EAC kernel (distrowatch.com, gamingonlinux.com). The installation image includes Linux kernel 7.3.5, and the project also provides a Windows Subsystem for Linux image (phoronix.com, linuxiac.com). Existing users switching to the new graphics-driver startup system must reinstall their driver profiles after updating, using the commands CachyOS recommends (linuxiac.com). AUR safeguards: Before building an AUR package, the new installer displays its PKGBUILD and install scripts, uses static analysis to flag lines for review, and shows changes between installed and updated versions (tuxmachines.org, distrowatch.com). Recovery options: The cachyos-recovery tool can boot Btrfs snapshots for testing and regenerates kernel, initramfs and bootloader files when restoring a snapshot (linuxiac.com, computerbase.de). Kernel module limits: DKMS modules do not work with the EAC kernel, so CachyOS supplies dedicated EAC packages for NVIDIA open and 580xx drivers, ZFS and the r8125 network driver (gamingonlinux.com).

title: CrowdStrike CEO: Companies are choosing between getting hacked and shutting down
description:
Microsoft systems down. Air traffic systems down. Problems at Chase, United, and Apple. After a week of outages across big systems, the AI conspiracy theories are in full swing. CrowdStrike founder and CEO George Kurtz describes how AI agents can turn a patch into a working exploit within an hour, and how CEOs are now taking services offline rather than risk being hacked. He also discusses CrowdStrike’s new AI Kill Switch, and why slowing down the frontier labs won’t slow down the attackers.

This is an abridged transcript of an interview from Rapid Response, hosted by former Fast Company editor-in-chief Robert Safian. From the team behind the Masters of Scale podcast, Rapid Response features candid conversations with today’s top business leaders navigating real-time challenges. Subscribe to Rapid Response wherever you get your podcasts to ensure you never miss an episode.

So what is going on? Over the past week, we’ve seen Microsoft systems go down. Air traffic systems go down. . . . The AI conspiracy theories are everywhere. Is all this just a coincidence?

I think a few of my friends and colleagues might have their tinfoil hats on as well. The reality is it’s the bill for the Mythos moment. Nine months ago, when Mythos came out, it really set in motion everyone looking for these vulnerabilities, right? And the whole industry has been racing to find as many vulnerabilities as it can and create as many patches as it can. But what we’ve done now is hit the sound barrier of actually being able to roll out all these patches. So when you look at what’s really taking place, and you look at all the issues that were found in Black October, you’ve got Darker November.

This is like the PHP code, and now Java, that people are scrambling to find and plug these gaps in.

Yeah, exactly. I think the Java one is actually going to be worse. There are already working exploits for all of that. But what people are doing now is rushing to roll out all of these patches, and they’re making the decision: Breach or break. That is, are we going to get breached because we can’t patch fast enough, or are we just going to break something and hopefully fix it if we roll it out? That’s kind of a new norm now because the industry can’t keep up.

Technology is messy. Things happen, and we’re going to get better and better as an industry at dealing with this sort of AI speed that we’re facing. When you think about all the legacy systems that are out there, and you think about even banking-type systems, there’s a lot of legacy-type code out there, and it’s not as easy just to create a fix while everything is in midstream. So it’s not always clear, and when things are melting down, you get on these 24-hour bridges, and people are trying to figure out what actually happened. It’s a bit of fog of war.

As you describe it and go through these examples, the air traffic one seems like a particularly fragile one. Is the system fragile?

I think technology is just fragile, whether you’re in an Apple ecosystem, Android, or you use Microsoft or Google, whatever you’re using. Every day people use this, and they sort of just expect it to work, and they should. But behind the scenes, when you actually look at how complicated these systems are, how they operate, and the interaction with hardware and software, disks get full, memory gets overloaded. You would think that all this has been worked out, but there’s a lot of just making stuff work in the background. And the technology folks, the men and women who have to keep this running, literally wake up every day and are just like, “OK, what are we going to have to deal with today?”

We’ve had other kinds of cyber troubles recently: OpenAI’s agents breaking into Hugging Face, and French supermarkets hit by hackers shutting down refrigeration systems, which seem like a different order of things. Are any of these episodes an “aha” moment for you, of us sort of crossing a threshold?

When you look at the latest Patch Tuesday from Microsoft, it was 1,000-plus vulnerabilities that were fixed. And again, this has spiked. . . . I think we’ve had 25% of all the vulnerabilities ever created found in the last year. Just to give you an idea of the order of magnitude of what we have to deal with.

So all these patches come out, and now what we’re seeing is the automation by AI agents and threat actors, where they will take a patch and compare what was patched versus what wasn’t patched, and they immediately know where the flaw was. Then they automate the vulnerability exploitation of that. Within an hour, you can have all that done, where that would take a nation-state actor maybe weeks to do.

So the fact that we’re starting to see these issues come up as quickly as we are, I’m not surprised. But when you think about the refrigeration systems, this was a big one in Europe. What does AI allow you to do? There’s probably a handful of people, relatively speaking, on planet Earth who understand how to program these refrigeration systems. But when you actually take an AI agent and go, “Hey, I don’t know much about the refrigeration system. You figure out how to program it,” it will figure that out. You don’t have to be an expert in any of these technologies now. And typically they’re underprotected because it’s a refrigerator. Nobody really thought about security when they were building it.

How much of the game is becoming like “My AI is better than their AI?” You have to stay ahead of the attacks.

It’s the old Spy vs. Spy cartoon. It’s really what it is, right? Who’s going to stay ahead?

You recently launched a product called the AI Kill Switch. Which is designed to stop rogue agents. How do you know which scenarios would prompt hitting the kill switch?

If you think about industry, if there was a manufacturing problem with a big machine, there’s always the red button. It’s like, stop that thing because it could be causing bodily harm. And it’s the same scenario. Are the agents doing something they shouldn’t be doing? Are they multiplying, attacking other systems, or bringing down systems internally? You want to be able to hit the button. The challenge with the kill switch is there’s blunt force. It’s almost like pulling the plug.

You work closely with both OpenAI and Anthropic. Dario Amodei at Anthropic has called on the industry to slow down. There’s been quite a lot of noise about it, although development keeps steaming ahead. Do you give OpenAI and Anthropic advice about speeding versus slowing?

At the end of the day, the genie is out of the bottle. You can slow whatever you want down on the frontier. The open-weight models are three months behind. Just slowing them down is not going to slow the rest of the world down. But keep in mind, and I just want to make this distinction, Bob, they are called labs. Okay, labs. What happens in a lab? You develop something, it kind of works, it does great things, but when you put it in the real world, it may not actually work as intended in the lab, which is why the security industry has now moved into the safety industry and has become a great opportunity for folks like us.

Anyone can slow down. If the model is not right, if it’s not aligned, if it’s not getting the output you want, if the quality control is not there, you know what you do? You don’t release it. You go back and do another run until you get it right.

So what should any business leader do right now to improve their cyber footing?

Well, I think maybe first is go find your security and IT people and give them a hug, because they are at 110% of capacity now. I’ve never seen this before, but it’s happening across industry. Company CEOs are making a decision: Take something offline or be hacked. They’re saying, “Hey, we would rather take a massive service offline than be hacked.” They’re willing to make that decision if it’s so bad. When PHP came out, I had plenty of companies say, “Hey, we may just take everything down because it’s so bad.”

title: Netanyahu's Likud demands rejection of Palestinian statehood in unity talks
description:
Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud says a proposed Israeli unity government should reject Palestinian statehood and retain Israeli-designated security zones in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria. The demands are part of Likud’s proposed framework as Gadi Eisenkot, the centrist Yashar party leader tasked with forming a government, invites Likud to intensive talks beginning Sunday, Nov. 22.

The October election left Eisenkot’s bloc with 48 seats, Netanyahu’s with 53 and Arab-led parties with 19 in the 120-seat Knesset; a majority requires 61. Likud also seeks an agreement with ultra-Orthodox leaders on military conscription, while members of Eisenkot’s camp disagree over whether to rely on Arab parties to form a government.

Eisenkot has said he would not serve in a government led by Netanyahu and could put a minority emergency government to a Knesset vote if broader coalition efforts fail. His mandate expires Dec. 6 and may be extended by up to 14 days.

title: The real surpasses 5.90 per dollar after Lula’s fiscal plan
description:
The Brazilian real surpassed 5.90 per dollar on Friday, November 20, while the São Paulo Stock Exchange and interest rates also reflected investors’ concerns about the fiscal adjustment by Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Brazil, Latin America’s largest economy, recorded a stock market decline during the week, and the dollar reached its highest level in more than a year.

The Senate approved the spending-containment and revenue-increase package, which aims to give the government budgetary leeway in 2027; financial traders consider it insufficient to address the deficit and public debt. In a livestream on Saturday the 21st, Lula defended the plan and denied that he would cut funds for health, education, or the minimum wage. The Chamber of Deputies was scheduled to debate it on Monday, November 23.

title: Medical AI studies report test results and validation gaps
description:
A Mayo Clinic team’s LENS vision-language model achieved 92.8% accuracy across 10 endoscopy interpretation tasks and outperformed 22 general-purpose AI models in tests on curated still images; the team’s report cautioned that accuracy may be lower in real-world use. A separate study found that Google DeepMind’s Gemini 3.0 Pro could update cancer symptom-management algorithms, but it omitted required content when revising depression guidance.

At Mary Free Bed in Grand Rapids, Abridge Scribe AI converts doctor-patient conversations into draft clinical notes, while an LSU project uses AI to monitor infants with artificial airways. Reviews found gaps in external validation for forensic dental AI and a lack of evidence that pulmonary-embolism AI has improved patient outcomes. LSU pediatric otolaryngologist Michael Dunham said “the decisions have to be made by humans based on the output of the AI”.

Exam results: Three language models scored between 89.9% and 91.3% on 1,310 anaesthesiology exam items; reviewers found that the book’s answer key was incorrect or contested for 59 of 81 disputed questions (bioengineer.org). Dental study topics: Among 20 forensic-odontology studies, dental age estimation was the most common topic, followed by human identification, biological-sex estimation and tooth classification (bioengineer.org). Publication growth: Of 590 pulmonary-embolism AI papers, 375 (63.6%) appeared in 2023–25; annual output in 2025 was about 14 times the 2017 total (bioengineer.org).

For the past several weeks, 100 Mile Ford has been taking part in the KOT Auto Group’s eighth annual Coat Drive, the third time the dealership has participated. Carole Velne, an accountant with 100 Mile Ford, said they are looking to collect as many coats, gloves, toques and other winter accessories as possible. “For those that need a little bit more extra warmth at this time of year. We collect coats, hats, toques, mitts and scarves,” Velne said. “We pile them up into our truck and at the end of November they will all be taken out to the Cariboo Christian Life Fellowship (CCLF) church in the 108 Mile Ranch area.” As of Wednesday, Nov. 18, Velne said the Ford Ranger they’ve been storing the donations in is half full. She noted that they would welcome more donations to come in for the last few days of November. To donate, Velne said community members simply need to come by 100 Mile Ford during their regular hours of operation and drop off their donations. She noted that some have left bags of clothes by the front door when they come in to work in the morning. “We know times are tough. The economy is not booming the best right now. There’s just a lot of people out there who really can’t afford the proper warm jackets for the Cariboo weather up here,” Velne said. “Whatever little bit people can throw our way is just such a big help.” Donations will be accepted until Monday, Nov. 30. Afterwards, they’ll go to the CCLF, which will be responsible for distributing them. Velne said she is looking forward to seeing just how much winter wear they can raise. “I think whatever people have that would keep people warm would be gladly accepted.” **News** **Doerkson lays out immediate priorities, explains B.C. cabinet

Eager to declutter, I recently went through my boxes of sentimental items. “I’m a minimalist,” I thought. “This should be easy.” Before long, I found myself holding a Ziploc bag filled with a dark substance, and I thought, “Oh yeah! The tar sands my uncle gave me. Well, I can’t just throw out these perfectly good tar sands, now, can I?” I spent most of that day sitting on the basement floor surrounded by my “thing piles”: keep, store, donate, recycle. It was a thoroughly exhausting day filled with micro-decisions. Somehow, we develop a strong emotional attachment to a thing, even as the thing holds absolutely no purpose in our lives. We may remember buying it, how proud we were of it, the effort it took to acquire it, or the hopes we had for it. When we hold the thing in our hands again, all those emotions come flooding back, and we hesitate to get rid of it, even though it has spent the last decade relegated to a box, at the back of a closet, in the room no one goes into. There are health implications of having too many things. Studies have linked clutter to sleep disturbances, digestive problems, poor food choices, and even relationship issues. On the other hand, having clean, minimalist spaces can make one feel light, relaxed, organized, and more productive. Beyond the mental health effects, it takes a financial toll, not just to acquire things, but to maintain, insure, and store them. And then there are the environmental effects. title: Hormuz ship attacks threaten Omani marine life as swimmer warns of pollution
description:
Repeated attacks on oil and gas carriers in the Strait of Hormuz risk contaminating marine habitats along Oman’s Musandam coast, including coral reefs and mangroves. Lewis Pugh, a British endurance swimmer and United Nations Environment Programme Patron of the Oceans, said chemical and oil pollution from damaged vessels could persist for decades and be difficult to remove.

Pugh swam about 15 kilometres in stages from the Musandam Peninsula around the Cape of Hormuz between Nov. 15 and 18. He said a tanker was struck about four kilometres away shortly after he entered the water, and he later saw a gas carrier engulfed in flames. The National reported more than 130 attacks on commercial vessels in the region since the conflict began on Feb. 28.

Iran has said it targeted ships it believed were using unauthorized routes through the strait; before the war, about a fifth of the world’s traded oil passed through it. Pugh called for an end to the fighting, the reopening of the waterway and a pollution cleanup.

title: Baltic ports carry 61% of Russia's October wheat exports
description:
Baltic ports handled 2.05 million of the 3.37 million tonnes of wheat Russia exported in October, raising their share to 61% from 52% in September. Shipments through Baltic and Caspian ports and to Central Asian countries together accounted for 80% of exports that month.

The rerouting follows interruptions to Black Sea and Azov Sea shipments. Andrey Sizov, director of the SovEcon analytical center, said damage to the Crimean Bridge has blocked the Kerch-Yenikale Canal, the only shipping route between the Azov and Black seas, and could delay the resumption of Azov Sea navigation while debris is cleared. Russia’s November wheat shipments are forecast at 2.9 million to 3.1 million tonnes, with weather and reduced river transport cited as possible constraints.

title: Microsoft details Outlook outage causes, consumer email losses and planned fixes
description:
Microsoft said a software defect introduced in July caused its Nov. 12 global Microsoft 365 outage, disrupting Outlook, Exchange Online and other services for about 12 hours. Its final incident report says the flaw affected network gateway servers and, under heavy load, stalled the process that handles incoming connections.

Microsoft confirmed it delivered all queued enterprise email, but some delayed messages to consumer Outlook mailboxes inactive for more than 30 days expired and bounced back to senders. It did not disclose how many messages were affected. The outage also delayed Microsoft Defender for Office protections and administrator actions, as well as policy and alert processing in Microsoft Purview.

Microsoft plans to limit Teams failovers to affected regions by the end of 2026 and separate gateway capacity by workload in the first quarter of 2027. It also plans to improve testing with traffic patterns that better reflect production systems.

title: Developers publish manifesto urging human review of AI-generated work
description:
Software developers and attendees at the AIE Code Summit published a “No AI Slop” manifesto on Nov. 22, urging people to take responsibility for AI-assisted work and review outputs according to the stakes. The signatories warn that AI agents can produce more code and documentation than a person can assess, while unchecked errors can be copied into later work.

A study of local open-weight models found that agents often identified the vulnerable code and formed a correct hypothesis but failed to produce a working input that would trigger the vulnerability. Separately, Together AI said an AI coding agent committed a repository credential that enabled an unauthorized party to download stored prompt samples. The company said it was continuing to review potentially exposed customer data.

Trace failures: A case study of 100 support-agent traces recorded 12 failures, including seven cases in which the agent asked for details instead of calling a tool and two involving misapplied policy rules (github.com). Security changes: Together AI said it made zero data retention the default for new accounts, added credential checks to pull requests and changed development rules for AI coding agents (together.ai). Model testing: Researchers tested 12 local model configurations on 10 vulnerability-reproduction tasks. Every configuration handled most of the six easier tasks, while the four harder tasks required the 27-billion-parameter model (arxiv.org). Review standard: The manifesto argues that success should be measured by what users receive and how it helps them, rather than code volume, merged pull requests or the number of agents running (github.com).

title: OpenRouter removes three AI providers after prompts exposed in breaches
description:
OpenRouter, a service that routes customer requests to third-party AI model hosts, removed three providers and revoked Zero Data Retention eligibility for 125 endpoints after researchers at Dragos found prompt data stolen from three inference providers. OpenRouter said it notified potentially affected customers and found no breach of its own systems. The 125 endpoints include precautionary removals, not 125 confirmed breaches.

Dragos seeded about two million prompts with unique links and test credentials from July through November 2026. Researchers found that credentials had been used to probe cloud accounts and that some requests marked for no retention had been copied or forwarded. One test link appeared in a workplace chat in China 24 days after it was sent. Providers can see prompts as they pass through a routing chain, and some requests were copied before a model processed them. OpenRouter said it was checking routing paths and would require assurances and validation before restoring endpoint eligibility.

title: South Korea’s education minister resigns after last-minute AI cheating measures cause confusion
description:
South Korean Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned Sunday after last-minute changes to anti-cheating rules caused confusion before the Nov. 19 national college entrance exam, known as the Suneung. President Lee Jae Myung accepted his resignation about an hour later. The changes followed a Nov. 15 confession by the top scorer on a national tax-accountant exam, who said he used a miniature camera and smartphone to cheat with artificial intelligence.

Authorities responded with device bans, stickers for clothing buttons, Wi-Fi restrictions and surprise emergency phone alerts. The annual exam carries high stakes for university admission and career prospects. Choi faced criticism for both the last-minute rollout and his statement to lawmakers on Nov. 16 that he was not confident he could stop AI-assisted cheating.

Officials identified 111 exam violations involving electronic devices, though not all necessarily involved AI cheating. President Lee tasked Prime Minister Han Seong-sook with overseeing follow-up measures, and the Education Ministry is reviewing cases before releasing scores Dec. 11.

title: COP31 draft sets 2035 electrification goal without clean-power rules
description:
A new COP31 draft sets a collective ambition to raise electricity’s share of global final energy use to 35% by 2035 and expand carbon capture, use and storage to gigatonne scale by that year. The text, drawn up by the Turkish and Australian summit co-presidents in Antalya, does not explicitly call for a transition away from fossil fuels or require the additional electricity to come from renewables. Governments had yet to approve it.

The electrification target concerns energy used across the economy, not a renewable-power quota. The latest draft also drops an earlier version’s direct link to tripling renewable capacity by 2030 and doubling the annual rate of energy-efficiency improvement.

The draft postpones decisions on a 2035 adaptation-finance goal and the timing of future Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) assessments, while noting those reports’ relevance to the 2028 global stocktake. The closing plenary was repeatedly delayed on Sunday as negotiators considered whether to adopt the text.

Science timetable: The draft highlights IPCC reports’ relevance to the 2028 global stocktake but leaves their publication schedule unresolved; India and Saudi Arabia favor waiting until 2029 (lemonde.fr, index.hr). Adaptation-finance demand: Developing countries sought

title: Rohingya groups demand sanctions as governments weigh Myanmar court ruling
description:
Rohingya organizations and governments are pressing for action after the International Court of Justice, the U.N.’s top court, found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya in 2017. A statement endorsed by 64 Rohingya groups urged the U.N. Security Council to enforce the judgment and called for sanctions, arms restrictions and limits on jet-fuel supplies. The groups said any return must be safe and voluntary, with citizenship and equal rights.

Myanmar is in a civil war, and the Arakan Army controls most of Rakhine State, including areas where many Rohingya would return. Myanmar’s government called the ruling unfair and pointed to the court’s 9-6 vote, while Malaysia said it respects the judgment and will engage with the U.N., the Organization of Islamic Cooperation and ASEAN on issues arising from it.

At the United Kingdom’s request, the U.N. Security Council is scheduled to hold closed consultations on the ruling on Nov. 25 and a private meeting on Dec. 7. Whether the council will take enforcement action remains uncertain; China and Russia hold vetoes.

title: El Salvador deploys 2,500 soldiers to Haiti without UN command
description:
Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele sent around 2,500 soldiers to Haiti to search for four aviation technicians who have been missing since October 18 and support operations against gangs. The mission began on October 28 under a bilateral agreement whose terms have not been disclosed; the troops operate outside the chain of command of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF).

Haitian and Salvadoran forces recaptured Sylvio Cator Stadium, which had been under the control of armed groups, and Salvadoran soldiers established a base there. The Bukele government says its troops will withdraw once they locate the four men, whose whereabouts remain unknown; meanwhile, Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé established a coordination cell on November 9, without publishing details about how it would operate.

title: SEC investigates Nvidia’s accounting practices
description:
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia’s accounting practices, according to people briefed on the inquiry. The investigation is at an early stage and could end without charges. Its precise focus remains unclear, including whether it concerns Nvidia’s geographic revenue reporting or financing arrangements with AI companies and data-center projects.

The SEC’s enforcement division recently created a financial-reporting and accounting unit. The Justice Department is reviewing Nvidia’s proposed $12.9 billion acquisition of open-source platform Hugging Face as part of a broader antitrust investigation.

title: Bambu Lab at Costco
description:
&&&

Bambu Lab at Costco · A1 Combo bundle · San Diego · November 21, 2026

Bambu Lab at Costco: What the $419.99 A1 Combo Bundle Gets You, and Who Fixes It When It Jams

Costco’s website sells a Bambu Lab A1 Combo bundle. We priced it against Bambu’s own store, read both return policies and Bambu’s warranty fine print, and mapped out who fixes what when it jams.

A 3D printer for sale a few clicks from the bulk paper towels still feels a little strange, but here we are. Costco’s site lists a Bambu Lab A1 Combo bundle, item 2066547, at $419.99: the A1 printer, its AMS lite four-spool feeder, four spools of Bambu’s PLA Basic, and two spare hotends. When we checked on November 21, 2026, it showed out of stock for delivery to a San Diego ZIP code and out of stock in-warehouse at a San Diego location.

So is it a deal? That turns on two things the listing doesn’t spell out: how much filament is on those four spools, and whether Bambu treats a Costco receipt like one from its own store. We repair Bambu printers across San Diego County, so we also cover the part nobody prices in: who fixes it when it jams.

$419.99Costco’s online price for the bundle, item 2066547, on Nov 21.
$359.00Bambu’s US store price for the A1 Combo alone the same day ($399.00 regular).
$9.25What each of the four spools has to be worth for the bundle to beat Bambu’s sale (our arithmetic).
1 yearThe warranty Costco’s listing states. Bambu’s 2-year US term is written for its own store’s buyers.

The short version

  • What you get: an A1 Combo (the A1 plus the AMS lite feeder), four PLA Basic spools, a 0.4 mm hardened steel hotend and a 0.2 mm stainless hotend. Bambu’s own A1 Combo box has 20 g of sample filament and the stock 0.4 mm hotend.
  • Price: at Bambu’s sale price, the printer and the same two hotends cost $382.98. The bundle costs $37.01 more, so the four spools have to be worth $9.25 each. Full 1 kg spools would be; the listing doesn’t give a weight (our arithmetic).
  • Only want the printer? Bambu’s store was $60.99 cheaper on Nov 21. At Bambu’s regular $399.00, the bundle wins before you count the spools.
  • Returns: Costco’s guarantee is the bundle’s strongest card. 3D printers aren’t on Costco’s 90-day electronics list, but the policy says limitations apply, so ask at the membership counter and keep the box.
  • Warranty: plan on 1 year from Bambu, not 2, and ask Bambu to confirm coverage on your serial number with the Costco receipt before anything breaks. Costco wasn’t on Bambu’s US reseller list when we checked.
  • Repairs: inside the warranty, open a Bambu ticket first. Hotends, nozzles, plates and PTFE tubes aren’t covered by anyone’s warranty, and that’s where we come in, along with setup ($159.99 for printers bought elsewhere), out-of-warranty repair and video help.

Five things the listing and the deal threads get wrong

The A1 isn’t enclosed.
Costco’s spec table lists the A1’s features as “Enclosured.” It’s an open-frame printer with a bed that slides front to back, and Bambu’s own FAQ says it doesn’t recommend enclosing the A1. Bambu lists PLA, PETG, TPU and PVA as the A1’s ideal filaments, and the moving bed needs clearance in front and behind.
Its top speed is 500 mm/s, not 550.
The listing gives 550 mm/s. Bambu’s spec page lists a 500 mm/s maximum toolhead speed and 10,000 mm/s² acceleration. Either way, that’s a ceiling, not the speed a typical print runs at.
Bambu’s 2-year US warranty is written for its own store.
Bambu moved US and Canada printers to two years in August. Its policy page, updated Sept 22, 2026, says that extension applies to products bought through Bambu Store US and Bambu Store CA. Costco’s listing says 1 year. Bambu also says only receipts from Bambu or “distributors authorized by Bambu Lab” count for warranty, and Costco wasn’t among the 48 US and Canada sellers on Bambu’s authorized reseller list on Nov 21. Ask Bambu to confirm your coverage in writing.
The $50 gift card is gone, and so is $50.
A July deal post listed the bundle at $469.99 with a $50 Bambu.com gift card. On Nov 21, Costco’s page showed $419.99 and no gift card in the box list. It’s the same math either way: $469.99 minus $50 of store credit is $419.99.
Skip the support email printed on the listing.
The address on Costco’s page has a typo in the domain. Bambu says warranty cases go through its support page, so start there.

What’s in the Costco box, and what’s in Bambu’s

Costco’s bundle is built on the same A1 Combo Bambu sells: the A1, a bed-slinger with a 256 mm cube of build space, plus the AMS lite, the open four-spool feeder that switches colors for you. The difference is what comes with it.

Item Costco bundle Bambu US store A1 Combo
Printer and feeder A1 and AMS lite A1 and AMS lite
Filament Four PLA Basic spools; the listing doesn’t give a weight 20 g of sample filament, random color
Hotends The A1’s pre-installed 0.4 mm stainless hotend, plus spare 0.4 mm hardened steel and 0.2 mm stainless hotends The pre-installed 0.4 mm stainless hotend
Gift card Listed in July; not in the box list on Nov 21 None
Price on Nov 21 $419.99 $359.00 sale, $399.00 regular
Shipping UPS Ground included Free in the 48 contiguous states

The spare hotends are the useful part. Bambu’s hotend page says its carbon-fiber PLA and PETG run with a low risk of clogging in a 0.4 mm hardened steel nozzle, and warns that filament filled with carbon fiber, glass fiber or metal is prone to clog a 0.2 mm nozzle. So the 0.2 mm hotend is for fine detail in plain filament, and the hardened one is for Bambu’s carbon-fiber PLA and PETG. When a swap is the fix, our A1 hotend guide walks through it.

The price math, two ways

Prices move every few days in late November, so treat these as a snapshot from Nov 21. All of it is our arithmetic on prices we read that day.

Line Price Where it comes from
Costco bundle $419.99 costco.com, item 2066547
A1 Combo at Bambu’s US store $359.00 Sale price; $399.00 regular
0.4 mm hardened steel A1 hotend $11.99 Bambu US store
0.2 mm stainless A1 hotend $11.99 Bambu US store
Printer plus the same two hotends $382.98 Our arithmetic
Left for the four spools $37.01 ($9.25 each) Our arithmetic
PLA Basic 1 kg refill at Bambu $14.99 list; $9.74 at 10+ rolls Bambu US store; refills come without a spool

Read it two ways. If you only want the printer, Bambu’s store was $60.99 cheaper on Nov 21, and Bambu’s 30-day return window and 2-year US warranty come with a store purchase. If you’d buy filament and a hardened steel hotend anyway, the bundle comes out ahead as long as each spool is worth more than $9.25. Four full 1 kg rolls would be worth $59.96 at Bambu’s refill list price and $38.96 at its 10-roll price, both above the $37.01 gap (our arithmetic).

Against Bambu’s regular $399.00, the bundle is already $2.99 cheaper before you count the spools. The catch is the weight: Costco’s page says four PLA Basic filaments and stops there. If they turn out to be small sample spools, the sale price at Bambu wins. The label on each spool will tell you; a kitchen scale will too.

Costco isn’t the only shelf with an A1 on it. Bambu’s reseller list includes Best Buy and Micro Center, and our budget multicolor roundup compares the A1 Combo with its rivals under $500. If multicolor is the point, read our purge waste guide too: every color change burns some filament, and it adds up.

Returns: Costco’s strongest card

Costco’s satisfaction guarantee promises a refund on merchandise you’re not happy with, with a short list of exceptions and no general time limit written into it. The exception that matters here is electronics, which get a 90-day window: televisions, projectors, major appliances, computers, touchscreen tablets, smart wearables, cameras, drones, camcorders, MP3 players and cell phones. 3D printers aren’t on that list.

The policy also says “Limitations apply” and points members to the membership counter. We read it as the general guarantee covering a printer, and we wouldn’t bet a purchase on that reading. We’re not lawyers. Ask at the counter before day 90 and keep the box. We read the policy the same way for the Creality K2 bundle Costco sells.

Online orders can go back to any Costco warehouse, and Costco says there are more than 800 of them, or you can start the return on costco.com. Bambu’s own return window is 30 days from delivery for its store’s buyers, and its policy says products bought from a reseller follow the reseller’s return and replacement rules. For a Costco unit, the return counter is the first stop for anything wrong out of the box.

What the counter can’t do is fix it. Costco’s Technical and Warranty Services offers free support for TVs, computers, tablets, cameras, appliances, home theater gear and printers, and nothing on that page mentions 3D printers. Call and ask, but expect to troubleshoot an A1 with Bambu’s support or with a local shop.

Warranty: what Bambu covers, and for how long

Bambu’s policy page gives a warranty term for every listed part of the A1 and the AMS lite. We drew it as a rack in the figure above: 34 parts at the full term, 4 at three months, and 14 with no warranty at all. That’s our count of the entries on Bambu’s two lists, so a part listed on both counts twice; filament and Maker’s Supply items are left out.

Part group Examples from Bambu’s list Bambu’s term First call
Main printer parts Mainboard, AC and TH boards, motors, belts, heatbed unit, touch screen, camera, fans 24 months* Bambu ticket
AMS lite main parts Mainboard, housing, feeder motor, filament hub, stand 24 months* Bambu ticket
Three-month parts Extruder unit (not its gears or sensor), AMS lite feeder unit, rotary spool holder, microSD card 3 months Bambu ticket, then us
No warranty Hotend with nozzle, heater, thermistor and sock; extruder gears; build plates; PTFE tubes; filament cutter; nozzle wiper; AMS lite funnels and spool claws None You, or us

*24 months is the term on Bambu’s US page, and its policy ties that term to Bambu Store US purchases. Costco’s listing says 1 year.

No warranty doesn’t mean no help. Bambu says it will replace consumables that fail from a manufacturing defect while the printer itself is in warranty, at its discretion. Wear is on you.

Bambu’s claim rules matter if you want a local repair. It wants a ticket through its support page first, with the receipt and photos, video or logs of the problem. It asks owners not to repair damage themselves without its guidance, and it says the warranty becomes invalid if an unauthorized service center works on the printer without its approval. That’s why, inside the warranty, we’ll ask you to open the ticket before we open the printer. If Bambu sends a part, ask on the ticket whether a local tech can install it, and we’ll do it once they say yes. Our support-ticket guide covers what to do when a ticket stalls.

Two more notes. Bambu says its terms don’t take away rights you have under state law, and California has its own warranty rules; we’re not lawyers. And if you’ve read about the A1’s 2024 recall over its heatbed cable, Bambu says A1 printers sold after January 30, 2024 already have the fixes, and Costco’s listing describes the reinforced cable.

What breaks on an A1 Combo, and who fixes it

Here’s how common A1 Combo problems line up with Bambu’s parts list, and what the parts cost on Bambu’s US store.

Problem Usual suspects Part and price Who handles it
Clog, thin or gappy lines Heat creep, damp or dusty filament, filled filament in the 0.2 mm nozzle A1 hotend: $9.99 (0.4 mm stainless) or $11.99 (0.4 mm hardened or 0.2 mm stainless) You can swap a hotend; there’s no warranty on hotends. We clear clogs on visits.
A blob of plastic around the hotend A print that lets go of the plate while the nozzle keeps extruding Heating assembly $19.99, silicone sock $2.99 (Bambu US store, Oct 22) Us, once it’s past the sock
AMS lite won’t feed or keeps retrying A tangled or cracked spool, a worn PTFE tube, the feeder unit PTFE tubes: no warranty. Feeder unit: 3 months Bambu in the first 3 months, then us
Prints won’t stick Fingerprints or wear on the plate, damp filament Build plates: no warranty You, with our plate guide
Layer shifts, grinding, a dead screen or board Belts, motors, the mainboard, the heatbed unit 24-month parts on Bambu’s list Bambu ticket first; us after the warranty

The details live in our guides: clearing a clogged Bambu, the blob of death, AMS feed problems, build plates that hold and when to swap an A1 hotend.

Your first week with a Costco A1 Combo

Do these in order. The first three cost nothing and save the most trouble later.

1Keep the box and every bit of foam

Costco’s return counter and Bambu’s warranty shipping both go easier with the original packaging.

Bambu’s policy says original packaging gives the best protection in transit, and that poor packing can mean extra repair charges or denied coverage for shipping damage. Don’t flatten anything until you know the printer is a keeper.

2Photograph the serial number and save the Costco order

Bambu asks for the receipt and evidence with every claim, so get both on file on day one.

Photograph the serial label and the box label, and save the costco.com order email as a PDF. If something fails in month eleven, you won’t be hunting for them.

3Ask Bambu to confirm your warranty

Open a ticket on Bambu’s support page with the Costco receipt and serial number, and ask what coverage applies.

Costco’s listing says one year, and Bambu’s 2-year US term is written for its own store. A written answer now beats an argument later. Save the reply with the receipt.

4Give the moving bed room

The A1’s bed slides front to back, so set it on a sturdy surface with clearance in front and behind.

A wobbly table shows up as ripples in prints. Our guide to 3D printer tables covers stands, load ratings and circuits.

5Update the firmware and bind the printer

Connect it to Bambu Handy or Bambu Studio and install the current firmware before the first real print.

Bambu sells region-specific printers and says one from the wrong region may not bind to an account or use cloud features. The Costco model number, PF002-A+SA005-US-COS, reads as a US unit; that’s our reading of the number, not Bambu’s.

6Run the calibrations and print one color first

Let the A1 run its full calibration, then print a single-color test before you load the AMS lite.

Bambu says the A1 calibrates its Z offset, bed level, vibration and nozzle pressure for every job. One clean single-color print tells you the printer is fine before color changes add variables.

7Load the AMS lite and keep the spares dry

Load the four spools, check that no PTFE tube is kinked, and seal up the spools you aren’t using.

The AMS lite is open to the room. Near the coast, marine-layer mornings mean damp air, and damp PLA strings and clogs. Keep spares in a sealed bin with desiccant.

8Label the spare hotends and learn the swap

Mark the 0.4 mm hardened steel and 0.2 mm stainless hotends and practice a swap while nothing is wrong.

Use the hardened steel hotend for carbon-fiber PLA or PETG and the 0.2 mm one for detail work in plain PLA or PETG. Put the stock hotend back for everyday printing.

Where Dreaming3D fits

We’re an independent repair shop in Carmel Valley, and where you bought the printer doesn’t matter to us. Here’s what we do for Costco buyers:

  • Setup: $159.99 per printer bought elsewhere, Costco included. We place it, calibrate it and run the first prints with you.
  • Repair: in person across San Diego County, $159.99 per printer, parts extra. Los Angeles by appointment; we confirm the date and price when you text.
  • Inside the warranty: we’ll ask you to open a Bambu ticket before we open the printer, and help you put together the photos, video and logs Bambu asks for.
  • Video help: live over Zoom or FaceTime, anywhere.
  • After Bambu’s warranty: our Lifetime Warranty plan is $24.99 a month for one printer, parts and labor, while the plan is active.
  • Printing instead: FDM at $7 a machine-hour and resin at $9, plus material, if you’d rather not own a printer at all.

What we don’t do: we don’t print metal, flight hardware, firearm components, load-bearing or safety-critical parts, or medical devices that touch patients.

A San Diego footnote: Costco’s own history says its first location opened in 1976, as Price Club, in a converted airplane hangar on Morena Boulevard. Bambu has no store of its own in San Diego that we know of (our Bambu retail post tracks where it’s opening), so for now a warehouse club is as close as Bambu retail gets here.

Common questions

Is the Costco Bambu Lab A1 Combo bundle a good deal?

It can be. On Nov 21 the bundle was $419.99, and the A1 Combo plus the same two hotends cost $382.98 on Bambu’s US store at its sale price. The four spools have to be worth $9.25 each to close the gap, which full 1 kg spools would be. If you only want the printer, Bambu’s store was cheaper. That’s our arithmetic on prices that change often.

What comes in the Costco Bambu Lab A1 Combo bundle?

Costco’s listing for item 2066547 lists the A1 printer with the AMS lite feeder, four PLA Basic spools, a 0.4 mm hardened steel hotend and a 0.2 mm stainless hotend. It doesn’t give the spools’ weight. A July version also included a $50 Bambu.com gift card; the Nov 21 box list didn’t.

Does a Costco A1 Combo get Bambu’s 2-year warranty?

Don’t count on it. Bambu’s policy page says the 2-year US and Canada extension applies to products bought through Bambu Store US and Bambu Store CA, and Costco’s listing says 1 year. Ask Bambu to confirm the coverage on your serial number with the Costco receipt.

Is Costco an authorized Bambu Lab reseller?

Costco wasn’t on Bambu’s US and Canada authorized reseller list when we checked on Nov 21. Bambu says only receipts from Bambu or distributors it authorizes are valid for warranty. The model number ends in -US-COS, which suggests a bundle packed for Costco, but that’s our inference. Ask Bambu before you rely on the warranty.

Can I return a 3D printer to Costco after 90 days?

Costco’s 90-day limit covers a named list of electronics, and 3D printers aren’t on it, so the general satisfaction guarantee appears to apply. The policy also says limitations apply. That’s our reading, not Costco’s answer, and we’re not lawyers. Ask at the membership counter and keep the box.

Is the Bambu Lab A1 enclosed?

No. Costco’s spec table says it is, but the A1 is an open-frame printer with a moving bed, and Bambu’s FAQ says it doesn’t recommend enclosing it. Bambu lists PLA, PETG, TPU and PVA as the A1’s ideal filaments.

Will Costco’s tech support help with a 3D printer?

Costco’s Technical and Warranty Services page lists free support for TVs, computers, tablets, cameras, appliances, home theater gear and printers, and doesn’t mention 3D printers. Call and ask, but expect to work through Bambu’s support or a local repair shop for A1 problems.

Will a local repair shop void my Bambu warranty?

It can, under Bambu’s terms. Its policy says the warranty becomes invalid if an unauthorized service center works on the printer without Bambu’s approval, and it asks owners to open a ticket before repairing anything. Inside the warranty, open the ticket first and get approval in writing. Outside it, any shop can work on it.

What isn’t covered by the warranty on an A1 Combo?

Bambu lists no warranty on the hotend and its parts, the extruder gears, build plates, PTFE tubes, the filament cutter, the nozzle wiper, and the AMS lite’s funnels and spool claws. The extruder unit and the AMS lite feeder unit get 3 months. Bambu says it may replace consumables that fail from a manufacturing defect while the printer is in warranty.

Do you fix Costco-bought Bambu printers in San Diego?

Yes, and where you bought it doesn’t matter. In-person repair across San Diego County is $159.99 per printer plus parts, setup for printers bought elsewhere is $159.99, Los Angeles is by appointment, and we help anywhere over Zoom or FaceTime. Inside Bambu’s warranty, we’ll ask you to open a Bambu ticket first.

Bought the Costco A1 Combo? We’ll set it up or fix it.

Text us a photo of the problem, or of the box if it’s still sealed. We’ll set it up, calibrate it and run the first prints with you, or come fix it, anywhere in San Diego County. Inside Bambu’s warranty, we’ll help you file the ticket first.

Book a visit

Or text 858-342-6984, email dreaming3dprinting@gmail.com, or message @dreaming3dprinting.

Setup is $159.99 per printer bought elsewhere; in-person repair is $159.99 per printer, parts extra. Los Angeles by appointment. We don’t print metal, flight hardware, firearm components, load-bearing or safety-critical parts, or patient-contact medical devices.

title: Canada wins China pork tariff relief, but offal remains taxed
description:
Canada secured tariff relief for some agricultural exports to China during Prime Minister Mark Carney’s visit for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, including the removal of a tariff on pork products. Pork offal remains excluded from the relief. The agreement also extends relief for some other products but is not a free-trade deal.

China is one of the largest markets for Canadian pork byproducts and among the few that buy them. The 25% tariff had made Canadian pork uncompetitive there. Federal Agriculture Minister Heath Macdonald and parliamentary secretary Cody Blois accompanied Carney on the trip. The agreement does not guarantee tariff relief beyond the current extensions.
