title: Windows Phone 7 – Emulator Automation
description:
Hi Folks,

In this next blog post we’ll review how to automate the Windows Phone 7 Emulator and what are some real-world usages this technique.

This blog post is the second blog post in a series of unrelated advanced Windows Phone 7 blog posts.
The previous blog post in this series is “Windows Phone 7 – Unlocked ROMs”.

 

Why is Windows Phone 7 Automation Important?

Currently, the Windows Phone 7 Emulator can only launch developer packages (XAPs) from inside Visual Studio 2010.
Meaning, if we’ve got a XAP we can’t get the emulator to load it without Visual Studio.

As we’ve seen in a previous blog post the emulator can be launched and even installed on machines that do not have Visual Studio. More on that here.
Let’s consider that in order to load XAPs into the Emulator we currently have to use Visual Studio. 

The problem is – How do we load XAPs into WP7 Emulators and Devices without using Visual Studio?

So how does our Build Server run nightly tests? Or how do our customers see our applications?

Customers and Build servers don't have Visual Studio 2010 installed.

So, how can we deploy XAPs to an emulator running on these machines?

 

Quit your Jibber-Jabber, show me how to automate the WP7 emulator!

Let’s create a new solution with a Console Application and a Windows Phone 7 Project.

We’ll use the ConsoleApplication as our automation harness that can run on any computer with the .Net framework.
The WindowsPhone Application is the application whose deployment we’ll automate.

 

The CoreCon 10 WP7 API

The secret sauce for WP7 Automation is the CoreCon API.
These CoreCon DLLs have been in deep hibernation since 2007 when they last got a major upgrade.
For WP7 Tools the CoreCon API has been updated and are used by Visual Studio 2010 when deploying applications to WP7 devices and emulators.

Let’s add a reference to Microsoft.SmartDevice.Connectivity.dll from the CoreCon API.
On a x64 developer box, the DLL can be found at: C:\Program Files (x86)\Common Files\microsoft shared\Phone Tools\CoreCon\10.0\Bin\Microsoft.Smartdevice.Connectivity.dll 

 

 

Now that we have the CoreCon DLL reference in place, we can start automating WP7.

Here’s the User Experience we’re aiming for in this demo:

We’ll have to build the following workflow:

     

We’ll start off by getting an instance of the WP7 CoreCon SDK instance to work with:

// Get CoreCon WP7 SDK

DatastoreManager dsmgrObj = new DatastoreManager(1033);

 

Platform WP7SDK = dsmgrObj.GetPlatforms().Single(p => p.Name == "New Windows Mobile 7 SDK");

 

Next up we’ll have to get a reference to either a WP7 physical device or a WP7 Emulator.
This demo will use the emulator, but if we set “useEmulator = false” this demo will try and connect to a physical WP7 device.

// Get Emulator / Device

bool useEmulator = true;

Device WP7Device = null;

if (useEmulator)

    WP7Device = WP7SDK.GetDevices().Single(d => d.Name == "Windows Phone 7 Emulator");

else

    WP7Device = WP7SDK.GetDevices().Single(d => d.Name == "Windows Phone 7 Device");

Now we’ll launch the WP7 Emulator/Device.
Note that the default WP7 Emulator Image is the one we’ll launch into, and in a previous blog post I’ve explained how to use the Unlocked ROM as the default ROM.

// Connect to WP7 Emulator / Device

Console.WriteLine("Connecting to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

WP7Device.Connect();

Console.WriteLine("Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device Connected...");

Next, we’ll have to check if our application is already installed, and if it is – we’ll uninstall it.
Since the the UpdateApplication Method in the current CoreCon API doesn’t work, this is our best bet on easily updating installed apps.

In order to Install or Uninstall our application, we’ll need it’s Application Product Identifier (GUID).
We can get the application GUID from the Properties/WMAppManifest.xml file.

 

We’ll write the code to check if an application is installed, and if it is – we’ll uninstall it.

Guid appID = new Guid("{5e75bba1-fbf6-463c-94ac-fa4a78f8fd12}");

RemoteApplication app;

if (WP7Device.IsApplicationInstalled(appID))

{

    Console.WriteLine("Uninstalling sample XAP to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

 

    app = WP7Device.GetApplication(appID);

    app.Uninstall();

 

    Console.WriteLine("Sample XAP Uninstalled from Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

}

At this point, we’ll install our XAP.
In order to do that, we’ll need 3 pieces of information:
1. The location of our XAP.
2. The Application GUID.
3. The location of the application icon.

// Install XAP

Console.WriteLine("Installing sample XAP to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

 

app = WP7Device.InstallApplication(

    appID,

    appID,

    "NormalApp",

    @"D:\visual studio 2010\Projects\ConsoleApplication1\WindowsPhoneApplication1\ApplicationIcon.png",

    @"D:\visual studio 2010\Projects\ConsoleApplication1\WindowsPhoneApplication1\Bin\Debug\WindowsPhoneApplication1.xap");

 

Console.WriteLine("Sample XAP installed to Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

The last step is to actually launch our application.

// Launch Application

Console.WriteLine("Launching sample app on Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

app.Launch();

Console.WriteLine("Launched sample app on Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

 

We’re done. And indeed when we run our sample application the app runs as expected:

 

So What is WP7 Automation good for?

There’s a lot of good use cases: Automating Unit tests, Loading Nightly builds into the emulator and even letting customers use the WP7 Emulator.
There’s really a plethora of reasons and situations WP7 Automation can prove useful in and it’s up to you to figure it out for your projects.

For instance in Vertigo, we’re using the WP7 Automation harness to run the WP7 Emulator on multi-touch laptops that our customers have.
So Vertigo’s customers, as part of an iterative process, get access to our current build without having to install or use Visual Studio 2010.

 

Access to Isolated Storage

One use-case in particular interests me, which is automating running all unit tests in the project after a Continuous Integration nightly build.

We can pretty much do all of the work to automate WP7 tests using WP7 Automation we’ve seen so far, but how do we get results into application? Or get instructions in?

The easiest method I can think off is communicate through cold storage – read & write files into Isolated Storage.

We’ll start off by writing a file into our WP7 Application IsoStore.
Remember that this code executes in the WP7 Emulator/Device.

public MainPage()

{

    InitializeComponent();

 

    SupportedOrientations = SupportedPageOrientation.Portrait | SupportedPageOrientation.Landscape;

 

    using (var isoStore = IsolatedStorageFile.GetUserStoreForApplication())

    using (var sw = new StreamWriter(isoStore.OpenFile("Foo.txt", FileMode.OpenOrCreate, FileAccess.Write)))

    {

        sw.Write("Hello WP7! (Written from WP7 IsoStore, read by Console Harness!)");

    }

}

Basically, We’ve written a Foo.txt file into our IsoStore and added some text into it.

Next, we would have used the RemoteIsolatedStorage class and get access to the emulator IsoStore, but that has not been enabled yet in CoreCon10.

We would have used RemoteApplication.GetIsolatedStorage() but that has not been implemented yet.

We’ll use a FileDeployer class instead.
There’s some reflection magic associated with getting a copy of a FileDeployer class that can be used for our application.

Thread.Sleep(10000);

//app.GetIsolatedStore(); <-- Throws NotImplementedException

object ConManServer = WP7Device.GetType().GetField("mConmanServer", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance).GetValue(WP7Device);

FileDeployer f = (FileDeployer)typeof(FileDeployer).GetConstructors(BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.NonPublic)[0].Invoke(new object[] { ConManServer });

Next, we’ll copy the Foo.txt file from the application isolated storage into our local binary folder and read it into the console:

f.ReceiveFile(@"\Applications\Data\" + appID + @"\data\isolatedstore\Foo.txt", @"\Foo.txt");

 

Console.WriteLine("\t" + File.ReadAllText(@"foo.txt"));

 

When we run this sample we can see the text written from IsoStore showing up on our console.

And we’re done, we’ve esteblished a two-way communication channel between WP7 Emulator/Device and Managed .net code.  

 

Console WP7 Automation Harness Source Code

Here’s the source code we’ve built in this project:

// Get CoreCon WP7 SDK

DatastoreManager dsmgrObj = new DatastoreManager(1033);

 

Platform WP7SDK = dsmgrObj.GetPlatforms().Single(p => p.Name == "New Windows Mobile 7 SDK");

 

// Get Emulator / Device

bool useEmulator = true;

Device WP7Device = null;

if (useEmulator)

    WP7Device = WP7SDK.GetDevices().Single(d => d.Name == "Windows Phone 7 Emulator");

else

    WP7Device = WP7SDK.GetDevices().Single(d => d.Name == "Windows Phone 7 Device");

 

// Connect to WP7 Emulator / Device

Console.WriteLine("Connecting to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

WP7Device.Connect();

Console.WriteLine("Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device Connected...");

 

 

Guid appID = new Guid("{5e75bba1-fbf6-463c-94ac-fa4a78f8fd12}");

RemoteApplication app;

if (WP7Device.IsApplicationInstalled(appID))

{

    Console.WriteLine("Uninstalling sample XAP to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

 

    app = WP7Device.GetApplication(appID);

    app.Uninstall();

 

    Console.WriteLine("Sample XAP Uninstalled from Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

}

 

// Install XAP

Console.WriteLine("Installing sample XAP to Windows Phone 7 Emulator/Device...");

 

app = WP7Device.InstallApplication(

    appID,

    appID,

    "NormalApp",

    @"D:\visual studio 2010\Projects\ConsoleApplication1\WindowsPhoneApplication1\ApplicationIcon.png",

    @"D:\visual studio 2010\Projects\ConsoleApplication1\WindowsPhoneApplication1\Bin\Debug\WindowsPhoneApplication1.xap");

 

Console.WriteLine("Sample XAP installed to Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

 

// Launch Application

Console.WriteLine("Launching sample app on Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

app.Launch();

Console.WriteLine("Launched sample app on Windows Phone 7 Emulator...");

 

Console.WriteLine("Reading Foo.txt Isolated Storage file:");

 

Thread.Sleep(10000);

//app.GetIsolatedStore(); <-- Throws NotImplementedException

object ConManServer = WP7Device.GetType().GetField("mConmanServer", BindingFlags.NonPublic | BindingFlags.Instance).GetValue(WP7Device);

FileDeployer f = (FileDeployer)typeof(FileDeployer).GetConstructors(BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.NonPublic)[0].Invoke(new object[] { ConManServer });

f.ReceiveFile(@"\Applications\Data\" + appID + @"\data\isolatedstore\Foo.txt", @"\Foo.txt");

 

Console.WriteLine("\t" + File.ReadAllText(@"foo.txt"));

 

Console.ReadLine();

 

Fin

In this blog post we’ve talked about why Automating the WP7 Emulator and Device deployment process is important and how to go about doing that.
Hopefully now you know how to automate WP7 XAP Deployment.

In the next blog post in this series we’ll talk about setting up a Continuous Integration build for WP7.

 

Leave a Comment

Are there any other use cases for WP7 Automation?
Are you planning on using this technique somewhere?
Was this a good blog post? Sound off in the comments.

 

Sincerely,

-- Justin Angel

title: European-Japanese BepiColombo enters Mercury orbit ahead of two-probe science mission
description:
BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, entered orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21, completing an eight-year journey and becoming the second mission to orbit the planet. The two orbiters remain attached; they are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10 and take up different polar orbits, with science operations due to begin in April 2027.

The mission will use the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, to study Mercury from separate vantage points. Their instruments are designed to examine the planet’s surface and interior, its magnetic field and the thin gas envelope around it, including how the magnetic field interacts with the solar wind.

Controllers in Germany confirmed the spacecraft’s capture several hours after a series of braking thruster firings, with the spacecraft about 152 million kilometers away. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival from December 2025. Its nominal science mission is planned to last one Earth year, with an extension through 2029.

excerpt: BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, entered orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21, completing an eight-year journey and becoming the second mission to orbit the planet (apnews.com, eos.org, mainichi.jp). The two orbiters remain attached; they are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10 and take up different polar orbits, with science operations due to begin in April 2027 (space.com, eos.org). The mission will use the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, to study Mercury from separate vantage points. Their instruments are designed to examine the planet’s surface and interior, its magnetic field and the thin gas envelope around it, including how the magnetic field interacts with the solar wind (eos.org, apnews.com). Controllers in Germany confirmed the spacecraft’s capture several hours after a series of braking thruster firings, with the spacecraft about 152 million kilometers away (apnews.com). A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival from December 2025. Its nominal science mission is planned to last one Earth year, with an extension through 2029 (eos.org). Orbital paths: Mio is headed for a highly elliptical polar orbit, while the European orbiter will use a less elliptical polar orbit (space.com). Long route: The spacecraft made one Earth, two Venus and six Mercury flybys to shed speed; the looping trajectory covered more than 10 billion kilometers (apnews.com, space.com). Energy challenge: Reaching Mercury is harder than reaching Pluto because a spacecraft must shed enough momentum to match Mercury’s path around the Sun (eos.org). Mission cost: The joint mission is valued at about $2 billion, or 1.7 billion euros (apnews.com, eos.org).
kite_context:
Perspective: Daniel Schmid, research-group leader at the Austrian Academy of Sciences’ Space Research Institute, said measurements of the strength and direction of Mercury’s magnetic field could help explain why the planet has a global field (orf.at). (ORF)
Quote: "What makes this mission really unique is that for the first time in space exploration, we are bringing two spacecraft to the vicinity of the planet, and we are going to put them in orbit around this mysterious body." (Santa Martinez, European Space Agency mission manager for BepiColombo, Eos)
Timeline: 21 November 2026: BepiColombo entered Mercury orbit after braking thruster firings (apnews.com, space.com).
Timeline: 9 December 2026: The European and Japanese orbiters are scheduled to separate (eos.org, space.com).
Timeline: 10 March 2027: The European orbiter is scheduled to reach its nominal science orbit (space.com, sapo.pt).
Timeline: April 2027: The mission’s science operations are scheduled to begin (eos.org, mainichi.jp).
Background: NASA’s Mariner 10 flew past Mercury in the 1970s. NASA’s MESSENGER was the only spacecraft to orbit the planet before BepiColombo, from 2011 until it ran out of fuel and struck the planet in 2015 (apnews.com, eos.org).

In a speech on Nov. 21, the eve of Lebanon’s 83rd Independence Day, he demanded that Israel withdraw, stop its attacks and return Lebanese detainees, while urging the Iran-backed armed group Hezbollah to hand over its weapons.

Aoun said the issues were linked and his government would pursue their resolution simultaneously. His address focused on Hezbollah, whose weapons have long exceeded the Lebanese army’s arsenal. The group has said it needs them to resist Israel.

A June agreement reached with U.S. mediation calls for Hezbollah to disarm, Israel to withdraw from southern Lebanese territory and the Lebanese army to deploy there. Implementation has stalled: Hezbollah has refused to surrender its weapons, and Israel continues to strike in Lebanon.

title: DietPi 10.9 adds support for five new single-board computers
description:
The DietPi project has released version 10.9 of its lightweight, Debian-based Linux distribution, adding images for five single-board computers: the Odroid C5 and Orange Pi 4A, Zero 4, 6 and 6 Plus. The Orange Pi 4A currently runs its processor cores at a fixed 768 MHz because of a kernel scheduling limitation; a proposed fix is under review.

The release also adds four applications, including Podman and Paperless-ngx, and introduces a Raspberry Pi fan-control utility. It improves Raspberry Pi temperature and voltage warnings and network reconnection. It also drops Readarr and Mono from the software catalog and disables installation support for Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr and Jackett on ARMv6 devices.

title: Earthquake in Peru leaves one dead, 16 injured and 853 affected
description:
The latest report on the magnitude 6.7 earthquake that struck central Peru on Friday put the toll at one dead, 16 injured, 853 people left homeless and another 529 affected. The deceased was a 45-year-old man who had been admitted to Hermilio Valdizán Medrano Regional Hospital in Huánuco; authorities did not specify the cause of his death.

The report counted 152 uninhabitable homes and 156 damaged ones, as well as damage to six schools, 22 health facilities, four churches, three community centers and about 300 meters of roads. Huánuco, Pasco and Junín sustained the most damage; Lima and Callao were also affected.

Authorities deployed medical personnel, ambulances, emergency response teams and technical crews, and coordinated humanitarian aid with local governments. In Huánuco, they sent machinery to clear roads blocked by rocks. Damage assessments and repairs to restore electricity are ongoing. The Geophysical Institute of Peru reported two subsequent earthquakes in Junín, with no new damage confirmed.

title: Tesla begins FSD v15 rollout with new driving display and safety claims
description:
Tesla has begun sending its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v15 software to early-access owners, adding a live, photorealistic visualization called Tesla Reality View and claiming a 25-fold improvement in handling safety-critical situations. The update also targets sign recognition, potholes, road debris, standing water and speed control near schools and in bad weather. Tesla says the supervised system can slow for detected speed cameras and adds a mode for cars carrying bike racks.

Reality View renders the surroundings from a virtual camera above the car and displays planned turns. Tesla says it lets drivers see and control what FSD intends to do. The company attributes the claimed safety improvement to an upgraded vision encoder trained on millions of internet videos, but has not published the underlying intervention rate, making the multiplier difficult to assess independently. Tesla chief executive Elon Musk said the wider release is planned for December with Tesla’s 2026 Holiday Update. Tesla has not identified which vehicles will receive the first general-release builds.

title: Finland restricts Gulf traffic as Baltic neighbors join ship rescue
description:
Finland took charge of maritime rescue and pollution-control operations after the Russian cargo ship Sparta II caught fire in the Gulf of Finland and drifted into Finnish waters on Saturday. Finnish officials said Ukraine was likely behind the drone strike; Kyiv had not commented. Authorities temporarily restricted air and sea traffic in the eastern gulf, while the Border Guard said the incident posed no danger to other shipping and reported no environmental damage.

Estonia sent a navy vessel to assist with firefighting and pollution response, and Swedish combat aircraft operating under Finnish command helped safeguard Finnish and NATO territory. A Russian rescue vessel also joined the operation, and Finland said it planned to allow the damaged ship to be towed back to Russian waters.

Hours after the strike, Finland reported that a Russian helicopter had entered its airspace by as much as 4.1 kilometers; Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen said it might have been involved in rescue or surveillance. The ship is linked to a Russian company providing services to the Defence Ministry, but Finnish officials said its cargo had not been confirmed and could include military material.

title: Former federal minister Navdeep Bains wins Ontario Liberal leadership
description:
Former federal industry minister Navdeep Bains won the Ontario Liberal leadership on Saturday, beating Toronto-area member of provincial parliament Lee Fairclough by 50.3% to 49.7% on the third ballot. Bains, who has no seat in the provincial legislature, said he intends to run for one but did not say where or when. He ruled out asking a sitting Liberal MPP to resign for him.

Bains takes charge of a party with 14 seats, behind the governing Progressive Conservatives’ 79 and the New Democrats’ 27. The Liberals have lost three straight provincial elections since Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s party first took office in 2018, and the next election may not come until 2030. Bains campaigned on jobs, economic growth and affordability, while his critics have pointed to his ties to former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau.

title: Bayer Roundup settlement leaves glyphosate debate over farm use unresolved
description:
A Missouri court’s approval of Bayer’s settlement over claims involving its Roundup herbicide does not alter Brazilian registrations for glyphosate products. U.S. farmers use glyphosate to control weeds after herbicide-tolerant soybeans and corn emerge, while Brazilian growers use it for weed control, including before planting in no-till systems. The judge approved a deal worth up to $7.25 billion on Nov. 20 to resolve claims by people who attribute non-Hodgkin lymphoma to exposure; Bayer denies the herbicide causes cancer.

Brazil’s health regulator retained the active ingredient after a reassessment, with risk-mitigation measures. In Europe, Italian farm group Coldiretti urged the European Union to stop imports of Canadian wheat dried with glyphosate, arguing that the practice is prohibited in Italy and the EU and disadvantages local growers.

title: African health summit adopts declaration setting 2027 accountability steps
description:
The second Dakhla Global Summit, a meeting on African health and social protection, closed in Morocco on Nov. 21 with participants from 30 countries adopting a declaration on access to care and stronger health systems. The declaration calls for vaccination, organized cancer screening, continuous care, local production of medicines and vaccines, and expanded health-worker training.

The summit’s follow-up plan calls for a first progress report at the 2027 meeting, which is also due to focus on equitable access to care, medicines and vaccines, as well as health data and artificial intelligence.

Three Salvadoran soldiers were killed and another was injured in an explosion while handling explosives at a camp; the contingent is also searching for four soldiers who have been missing since an ambush on October 18. Police say they are seeking to reclaim areas controlled by the gangs.

title: New operator and successor cloud firm widen Nvidia chip-smuggling probe
description:
Li Ming, a 52-year-old Chinese businessman, was a central operator in a network suspected of routing restricted Nvidia AI chips to China, with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang serving as its public face, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the operation. Singapore charged Li in February 2025 with fraud over claims that servers he bought would be used by his Singapore company; the indictment did not name Megaspeed.

The reporting also describes a successor venture, NovaGate Cloud, formed in 2025 by people linked to Megaspeed. NovaGate says it operates data centers using Nvidia’s latest Blackwell chips. Shipping records reviewed by the Journal show at least $300 million in Nvidia-equipped hardware imports through a Malaysian affiliate in the first five months of 2026.

A separate investigation linked companies associated with Alice Huang’s family and associates to about $3.6 billion in Chinese state funding, while noting that it remains unclear whether China’s military used the computing capacity. Former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before House committees behind closed doors on Dec. 1; a Senate office requested public testimony for Dec. 3.

title: Suspected tainted liquor kills 16 in Manipur, 600 hospitalized
description:
At least 16 people have died and about 600 have been hospitalized after drinking suspected adulterated liquor in Manipur’s Chandel district, state officials said. Twelve patients were in intensive care. Police arrested six people as investigators traced the liquor to Sugnu in neighboring Kakching district.

The precise cause of the deaths and whether the liquor contained methanol remain unconfirmed pending medical findings and laboratory tests. Patients have been treated at hospitals in Imphal and the affected districts. Officials sent medical teams to Chandel and urged residents to avoid liquor from questionable sources.

Manipur has formed a four-member inquiry committee to examine the liquor’s origin and composition, medical and forensic evidence, and possible regulatory failures. The panel must report within one month. Police and excise teams have also been directed to inspect sales and production sites, seize illegal liquor and collect samples for testing.

title: Pentagon restricts US-Canada defense ties in classified memo
description:
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a classified directive restricting military cooperation with Canada. Republican Sen. Mike Rounds said it limits informal and social contact between the countries’ military personnel. The Washington Post reported that the memo circulated last week but said it had not seen the document. The directive’s full scope remains unclear.

The Pentagon says the guidance refocuses engagement on U.S. defense priorities and will not affect military intelligence sharing, the North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD) or cooperation through the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO). Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty said he had not seen the memo and had observed no change in military cooperation.

President Donald Trump has imposed tariffs on Canadian goods, criticized Canada’s defense spending and repeatedly suggested that Canada become a U.S. state. The Pentagon paused a longstanding bilateral defense forum in May, while Canada says it has reached NATO’s 2% spending target and plans to increase defense spending to 5% of gross domestic product by 2035.

title: Montreal police make first arrests in force misconduct probe
description:
The first criminal arrests in a Montreal police misconduct investigation have prompted civil-rights advocates to call for accountability and wider scrutiny. One said the case could set a precedent for holding officers responsible. Allegations involving a second station, downtown Station 21, include mistreatment of unhoused people and a claim that an officer urinated on someone while on duty.

Quebec prosecutors charged former Montreal police officers Vincent Routhier and Zachary Belzil with assault and breach of trust; Belzil also faces a criminal-harassment charge. Both were released on promises to appear, and no court date had been set. The force’s union is challenging the administrative dismissals of seven officers, and Chief Fady Dagher has said they could be reinstated if those challenges succeed. Related criminal investigations continue under the supervision of an independent observer appointed by Quebec’s public security ministry.

The force’s union is challenging the administrative dismissals of seven officers, and Chief Fady Dagher has said they could be reinstated if those challenges succeed (montrealgazette.com). Related criminal investigations continue under the supervision of an independent observer appointed by Quebec’s public security ministry (thestar.com, montrealgazette.com). Other allegations: A Station 39 officer was accused of deleting evidence from a domestic-violence victim’s phone after recognizing the alleged abuser (thestar.com, montrealgazette.com). Street checks: The Red Coalition says street checks enable racist and discriminatory policing and is calling on Montreal’s police service to end the practice (cbc.ca). Dismissal process: Montreal police revoked the seven officers’ security clearances, allowing the force to dismiss them before criminal or disciplinary proceedings concluded (montrealgazette.com).

Perspective: Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada: She said people who come forward must be heard and taken seriously. She thanked officers who broke what she called the code of silence (thestar.com). (The Canadian Press via Toronto Star)
Quote: "It validates everything we had hoped would take place" (Fo Niemi, executive director of the Center for Research-Action on Race Relations, CBC News)

Supply-chain participants discussed contract-based partnerships, while a deputy agriculture minister called for stronger market monitoring.

Popielewicz's company handled about 5,000 tonnes of pumpkin seeds last year and is targeting up to 9,000 tonnes this year, depending on the harvest.

title: US panel says China aided Pakistan to constrain India's rise
description:
The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission said in its 2026 report, released Nov. 18, that China backed Pakistan during the May 2025 India-Pakistan fighting after India launched Operation Sindoor. The commission said Beijing showed it could strengthen Islamabad without entering combat, complicating Indian military planning and heightening concern about a two-front threat.

The report describes that support as part of broader military, economic and maritime pressure intended to constrain India’s power. It says Pakistan used advanced Chinese-supplied weapons. Chinese state media later aired an engineer’s account confirming that Chinese personnel provided technical support in Pakistan during the conflict. The commission urged Washington to move beyond periodic exercises to sustained maritime and intelligence coordination with New Delhi, while noting that India’s strategic autonomy means closer ties will not guarantee alignment with U.S. objectives.

title: Battlefield use of AI weapons grows as Geneva talks leave rules unsettled
description:
AI-enabled weapons are in use in conflicts in Ukraine, Sudan and the Middle East, while campaigners say armed drones that can independently select and strike targets have appeared in limited cases. The International Committee of the Red Cross says commanders must remain responsible for the lawful use of force.

At U.N.-backed talks in Geneva, 128 countries agreed to develop an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons over the next two years, but left open whether it would be legally binding. Around 100 countries had sought binding rules; the United States, Russia and Israel opposed that push, and the consensus-based forum allowed any member to block stronger language.

The process is expected to examine which systems should be prohibited and which could be regulated. Government experts are to recommend the instrument’s form, including whether it should be binding. The International Committee of the Red Cross says commanders must remain responsible for the lawful use of force, including when weapons act with little or no human oversight.

title: Saturn 4 Ultra 16K LCD Connection Error: Cable, Firmware, Screen or Mainboard? How to Tell, and What to Buy
description:
&&&

Repair guide · Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K · Updated November 20, 2026

Saturn 4 Ultra 16K LCD Connection Error: Cable, Firmware, Screen or Mainboard? How to Tell, and What to Buy

The self-check flags the LCD screen connection. Before you buy a screen, rule out the ribbon cable and the firmware, which take seven screws to check instead of fifty-eight.

Your Saturn 4 Ultra 16K boots, runs its self-check, and one line comes back failed: the LCD screen connection. The screen is the expensive, obvious suspect, and Elegoo will sell you a new one for $129.99. But the same message can come from a ribbon cable that has slipped in its latch, or from firmware that doesn’t match your mainboard. You can check both with the back cover off, which is 7 screws. Getting a new screen in takes 58.

We print customer jobs on a Saturn 4 Ultra 16K in our San Diego shop, and we repair Elegoo resin printers in person around San Diego County. This guide takes Elegoo’s own procedures and puts them in the order we’d work through them, cheapest first. It also covers the parts, part numbers and warranty terms as they stood on November 20, 2026.

The short version

  • What it means: the mainboard isn’t getting the answer it expects from the 10-inch exposure screen under the vat. There are four suspects: the ribbon cable, firmware that doesn’t match the board, the screen itself, and the mainboard.
  • Check in order of screws: 0 (power-cycle, firmware version, exposure-test photo), 7 (board revision, firmware match, reseat the ribbon at the board), 48 (the ribbon at the screen) and 58 (a new screen).
  • 16K parts are not 12K parts: the 16K screen (A0S0V1, $129.99), mainboard (A0S061) and firmware are their own. The Saturn 4 Ultra screen ($114.99) and its firmware file don’t belong in a 16K.
  • Warranty: Elegoo covers the screen for 3 months and the machine for 12, counted from when your order arrived. Leaks and third-party repairs are excluded. If you’re inside either window, email Elegoo before you open the printer.
  • Local help: in San Diego County we can do every step on-site. Los Angeles visits are by appointment. Anywhere else, we can walk you through it over video.

Three things people get wrong about this error

“An LCD error means the screen is dead.”
Not necessarily. Elegoo’s own LCD display guide lists a badly seated or damaged ribbon cable and outdated or incompatible firmware as causes, alongside a failed screen. It has you reseat the cable at both ends and update the firmware before contacting support.
“Saturn 4 Ultra parts fit the 16K.”
Some do. Elegoo sells the same build plate and release film for the Saturn 4, 4 Ultra and 4 Ultra 16K. The screen, mainboard and firmware are different. Elegoo sells a separate 16K screen and publishes separate 16K firmware, and Printer Hub reports that 12K firmware makes a 16K stop recognizing its screen.
“Elegoo’s wiki has a fix for this.”
Not a specific one. On November 20, 2026, Elegoo’s 16K wiki page listed five self-test error guides: resin tank, X-axis motor, auto-leveling, foreign matter and mechanical sensor. None covers the LCD line. The nearest official procedure is the general LCD Screen Display Issue page, which covers all of Elegoo’s LCD printers.

What the self-check is actually telling you

At power-on, and whenever you run it by hand, the 16K checks its hardware and lists each item with a status. Printer Hub’s reference table names the line “Status of LCD screen connection”; the exact wording can vary between firmware versions. Elegoo’s manual says only that the printer checks key hardware at startup, and that you should follow the on-screen prompts and not touch the machine while it runs.

The 16K has two screens. One is the touch screen you tap. The other is the 10-inch, 15120 × 6230 mono LCD under the vat, which masks the UV light into each layer. This error is about the second one. If the touch screen is stuck on the ELEGOO logo, that is a different fault, and Elegoo has a separate guide for it that blames firmware corruption or a short circuit.

Read the symptom before you pick up a hex key

What you see Most likely Start here
LCD line fails right after a firmware update Firmware that doesn’t match your mainboard revision Device Information (0 screws), then the capacitor check (7 screws)
LCD line fails after the printer was moved, shipped or opened for another repair Ribbon lifted or crooked in its latch Reseat it at the mainboard (7 screws)
LCD line fails right after a new screen went in Ribbon not fully seated or latched at one end Reopen and seat both ends; check any end markings
LCD line fails after a resin leak Resin on or in the screen or a connector Stop powering it on; read our resin leak guide
Self-check passes and the exposure test shows the image, but nothing cures Not this fault: the UV light path Elegoo’s UV light guide; the adapter should read 24 V, 6 A
Exposure test shows part of the image, lines or dead pixels The screen, or a damaged cable Photograph it; our Saturn 4 Ultra errors guide covers dead pixels
Touch screen stuck on the ELEGOO logo Firmware corruption or a short, not the LCD line Elegoo’s recovery firmware steps

One trap worth knowing: Elegoo says the 16K needs a 24 V, 6 A adapter, and that a 12 V Mercury wash-and-cure adapter plugged in by mistake stops the UV light from working. If both bricks share your bench, read the label.

1Check before you open anything (0 screws)

These cost nothing and tell you which branch you’re on.

  1. Power-cycle and watch the check. Turn it off at the switch, wait, turn it on, and let the self-check run without touching the printer. Note whether the LCD line fails every time or only some of the time.
  2. Write down when it started. After a firmware update, a move, a leak or a screen swap? The table above points each one at a different first step.
  3. Read the firmware version. Go to Touch Screen > Device Information and note whether the version ends in the letter B. You need this at the next step.
  4. Run the exposure test and photograph it. Take out the vat and plate, run Tool > Screen Exposure (some Elegoo pages call it Tool > Exposure) with the ELEGOO pattern, and photograph the screen. Is it blank, partial or normal? Elegoo support asks for a photo of the screen not exposing and one during exposure.
  5. Find your order number. If you bought from a distributor, find the invoice instead. Elegoo asks for one or the other.

Wear nitrile gloves whenever the vat is out. Uncured resin is a skin irritant, and resin on your fingers ends up on ribbon contacts.

2Check behind the back cover (7 screws)

Power off and unplug the adapter. Take out the 7 screws on the rear cover with a 2.0 mm Allen key. That exposes the mainboard and the mainboard end of the LCD ribbon.

  1. Identify the board revision. Elegoo’s X-axis self-test guide has you check whether a capacitor is fitted to the mainboard. Printer Hub describes a pair on the right side of the board. Take a sharp photo of the whole board: Elegoo asks for one, and the right firmware file depends on it.
  2. Match the firmware to the board. See the firmware panel below. A board with the capacitor needs firmware ending in B, installed from a USB drive. A board without it updates over the air.
  3. Reseat the ribbon at the mainboard. Peel off the tape over the ribbon, lift the latch and slide the cable out. Look for creases, tears, scorch marks or resin on the contacts. Slide it back in straight and all the way, press the latch down, and tape it again. Elegoo’s guide for its sibling Jupiter 2 asks for the cable to sit parallel to the latch. On cables with marked ends, the end marked LCD or SCREEN faces the screen and the end marked MB faces the mainboard.
  4. Close up and retest. Refit the back cover with all 7 screws. Elegoo’s reassembly step mentions only five; put back what you took out. Power on, then rerun the self-check and the exposure test.

Firmware: match it to the board

What you find What to do
Capacitor fitted, version ends in B Nothing to change. The firmware matches, so move on to the ribbon.
Capacitor fitted, version doesn’t end in B Update from a USB drive with Elegoo’s B file for the 16K: Saturn 4 Ultra 16K Firmware-V1.4.4B-20251023-V8. Elegoo’s page lists the 12K file, Saturn 4 Ultra Firmware-V1.4.5B-20251028-V4, on the next line. Don’t grab that one.
No capacitor Update over the air. Elegoo’s download center has no firmware file for the 16K and recommends OTA.
Won’t boot after an update Use Elegoo’s recovery file, ChituUpgrade.bin, in the root folder of a FAT32 USB drive smaller than 16 GB, then update again.

Never load Saturn 4 Ultra (12K) firmware on a 16K. Printer Hub reports that the printer then stops recognizing its screen, which produces exactly the error you’re trying to fix.

Stop here if a connector looks scorched or has resin on it. Photograph it, leave the printer off, and contact Elegoo or a repair shop. Powering a contaminated board can turn a cable job into a mainboard job.

3Reach the screen end of the ribbon (48 screws)

Elegoo’s general guide says to check the cable at the screen as well as at the board. On the 16K, the only route Elegoo documents to that end is its LCD replacement procedure. The screen’s circuit board comes within reach once the base is off, which is screw 48 by our count: back cover 7, UV housing 7, cover tops 10, cover bottoms 10, base 14. On the way you unplug the touch screen ribbon, the camera, the LED, the Wi-Fi antenna and the UV board plugs, and you cut the cable ties.

So this is where you decide whether to keep going yourself:

  • Still inside Elegoo’s window? That’s 12 months for the machine and 3 for the screen. Email 3dp@elegoo.com with the evidence listed in the warranty section before you go further. Elegoo’s policy excludes printers repaired by a third party or modified by the owner.
  • Out of warranty and comfortable with ribbon latches? Carry on. Have fresh tape and cable ties ready, because you’ll cut the old ties.
  • Not comfortable? This is a sensible place to hand it off. See the local help section below.

Elegoo asks for a photo of the QR code on the screen, and its policy excludes LCD screens without an identifiable serial number. Don’t peel or scratch that label, on the old screen or the new one.

4Replace the screen (58 screws, $129.99)

Replace the screen if the exposure test is still blank or partial after you’ve reseated both ends of the ribbon and matched the firmware, or if you can see cracks, lines or dead pixels.

  1. Back of the printer. Power off and unplug. Take off the back cover (7 screws, 2.0 mm). Free the LCD ribbon at the mainboard. Unplug the LED and camera plugs, and pull the Wi-Fi antenna with tweezers.
  2. UV housing. Lift the UV enclosure and raise the camera slightly. Take out the 6 screws under the housing assembly and the 1 at its back (2.5 mm), then lift it away.
  3. Side and front covers. Remove the 10 screws along the edge of the middle panel. Then remove the bottom screws of the right (3), left (3) and front (4) covers. Open the front cover gently, because the touch screen ribbon is still attached. Untape and unlatch it.
  4. Base. Cut the cable ties, unplug the UV light board and mainboard plugs, and remove the base (14 screws).
  5. Old screen out. Peel the tape along the screen’s edge and cut the ties on its circuit board. Remove the Fresnel lens (10 screws) without touching its surface. Push the screen forward out of the middle panel and clean the old double-sided tape off the frame.
  6. New screen in. Fit the new ribbon to the screen’s board, latch it and tape it. Put double-sided tape on the lower frame and peel the protective films. Seat the screen glass side down, hold the X-axis while you press the edges, then tape the edge.
  7. Everything else back. Refit the Fresnel lens (10), the ties on the screen’s board, the base (14), the side and front covers, the touch screen ribbon, the housing assembly, the plugs and the back cover.
  8. Verify. Power on and run Tool > Exposure > ELEGOO. The logo should show cleanly. If the LCD line still fails, the first suspect is the ribbon you just seated.

That’s Elegoo’s sequence, shortened. Watch Elegoo’s video and keep its page open while you work. It shows which plug is which better than any description.

5When it’s the mainboard

Suspect the board last. That means a known-good screen and a good, properly seated ribbon still fail the check, with firmware that matches the board. Elegoo publishes no test that isolates the board for this line, so in practice the proof is substitution: the fault stays when everything around the board has been swapped or ruled out. Elegoo does publish a general board-health check in its stuck-on-logo guide. With every cable except the touch screen ribbon unplugged, a printer that still can’t reach the main menu probably has a faulty board.

The 16K board is A0S061. Printer Hub gives the Saturn 4 Ultra (12K) board as A0S071. On November 20, 2026, Elegoo US’s Saturn parts page listed 21 products: screens, build plates, release film and so on. It had no 16K mainboard and no separate LCD ribbon cable. Ask Elegoo support for the board, and send the board photo so they match the revision.

Elegoo’s motherboard procedure goes in from the back and the right side. It numbers 23 screws (back cover 7, back cover holder 6, right side cover 3 and 3, board 4) plus some holder screws it doesn’t count. You pull hot-melt glue off the connectors with pliers, move the two shading plates to the new board, and latch and tape both ribbons. The printer runs its self-check when you power it back on.

Elegoo US ships free on orders of $50 or more to the 48 contiguous states and DC, in 3 to 7 business days. The 16K itself lists at $649.99 and is $399.00 in Elegoo’s Black Friday sale this week. If you print daily and you’re buying a 16K now, Elegoo’s product page offers the same screen as a $91.00 add-on (30% off), but only bought together with a printer.

Part Elegoo US coverage

Periods run from the date your order was received. Within 14 days, Elegoo can refund, replace or repair a quality problem. After that, while you’re in warranty, the remedy is repair, and Elegoo pays the repair fee. Parts you buy separately get the same policy as the machine. The exclusions include products repaired by a third party or modified by the owner, and LCD screens without an identifiable serial number. Source: the Refund & Warranty tab on Elegoo US’s 16K page.

Three months isn’t long for a screen. At 4 hours of printing a day, it covers about 364 hours, or 18% of Elegoo’s 2,000-hour figure. That’s our arithmetic. Printer Hub’s known-issues list includes owner reports of screens failing at 100 to 200 hours, which falls inside that window. If yours is young, email Elegoo first.

On third-party repair: the FTC says a company that voids your warranty because you chose an independent shop may be breaking federal law. A company can still refuse to cover damage that the outside repair caused. We’re not lawyers, and this isn’t legal advice. Our practice is simple: if your printer is still inside Elegoo’s window, we’ll ask you to contact Elegoo before we open it.

What Elegoo asks for with an LCD problem

  • A photo of the screen when it isn’t exposing, and one during the exposure test
  • A photo of the LCD ribbon connection at the mainboard
  • A photo of the LCD ribbon connection at the screen
  • A photo of the QR code on the screen
  • Your order number, or the distributor’s invoice
  • Also useful for this fault: the firmware version from Device Information and a photo of the mainboard

In San Diego or Los Angeles? We can do this on-site

  • San Diego County: in-person service is $159.99 per printer, parts not included. We work through the checks in this order and tell you what we found before anything gets ordered.
  • Los Angeles: visits by appointment. We confirm the date and price when you text.
  • Anywhere else: live help over Zoom or FaceTime. Most of the 7-screw checks work well over video, with you holding the camera and us reading the board. We confirm the price before the call.

Common questions about this error

What does the LCD screen connection failure in the Saturn 4 Ultra 16K self-test mean?

It means the mainboard isn’t getting the response it expects from the 10-inch exposure screen under the vat. The usual suspects are the LCD ribbon cable, firmware that doesn’t match the mainboard revision, the screen itself, and, last on the list, the mainboard. It isn’t about the touch screen you tap.

Does the LCD connection error mean my screen is dead?

Not necessarily. Elegoo’s own LCD display guide lists the ribbon cable and outdated or incompatible firmware as causes and has you reseat the cable and update firmware before contacting support. Both can be checked behind the 7-screw back cover. A new screen means 58 screws out by our count of Elegoo’s steps.

Can I use a Saturn 4 Ultra (12K) screen or firmware in the 16K?

No. Elegoo sells a separate 16K screen (A0S0V1, $129.99) and publishes separate 16K firmware. Printer Hub reports that the 12K screen doesn’t fit and that 12K firmware makes a 16K stop recognizing its screen. The build plate and release film are the parts that are shared.

How do I know which firmware my Saturn 4 Ultra 16K needs?

Check Device Information to see whether the version ends in B, then take off the back cover and check whether a capacitor is fitted to the mainboard. Elegoo says boards with the capacitor need the B firmware from a USB drive (Saturn 4 Ultra 16K Firmware-V1.4.4B-20251023-V8). Boards without it update over the air.

How much does it cost to fix a Saturn 4 Ultra 16K LCD connection error?

Reseating the ribbon and matching the firmware cost nothing in parts. A new 16K screen is $129.99 from Elegoo US ($91.00 only as an add-on bought with a printer). Elegoo US doesn’t list the 16K mainboard (A0S061), so ask Elegoo support for it. Our in-person service in San Diego County is $159.99 per printer, parts not included.

Does Elegoo’s warranty cover the Saturn 4 Ultra 16K LCD screen?

For 3 months from when your order was received, according to Elegoo US’s policy. The machine gets 12 months. The screen warranty excludes resin leakage, damage to the scratch-resistant film, and man-made or collision damage, and Elegoo excludes LCD screens without an identifiable serial number.

Will opening my Saturn 4 Ultra 16K void the warranty?

Elegoo’s policy lists products repaired by a third party or modified by the owner among its exclusions. The FTC says companies that void a warranty because you used an independent shop may be breaking federal law, but they can refuse to cover damage the outside repair caused. If you’re inside Elegoo’s window, contact Elegoo first. This isn’t legal advice.

Can Dreaming3D fix a Saturn 4 Ultra 16K in San Diego or Los Angeles?

Yes. In-person service in San Diego County is $159.99 per printer, parts not included. Los Angeles visits are by appointment, and we confirm the date and price when you text. Anywhere else, we offer live help over Zoom or FaceTime. Text 858-342-6984 or book at dreaming3d.net/pages/repair-request.

Send the self-check screen, the exposure-test photo and your firmware version. We’ll tell you which branch you’re on before anyone takes out a screw.

Book a repair

Or text 858-342-6984, email dreaming3dprinting@gmail.com, or message @dreaming3dprinting.

title: France protests enter sixth weekend as turnout falls and clashes flare
description:
Protesters in France demonstrated over living costs and public services for a sixth consecutive Saturday on Nov. 21, with the Interior Ministry counting 82,500 participants nationwide and organizers estimating 150,000. Both figures were down from the previous weekend and far below the 800,000 organizers said had joined the first large march on Oct. 17. Students, unions, left-wing groups and Yellow Vest activists marched over living costs, housing, education and public services. Protesters also opposed a new law expanding legal protections for police who use firearms.

Most marches were peaceful, but police used tear gas to disperse unauthorized gatherings in Lyon, and clashes and fires were reported in several cities. The Interior Ministry reported 144 arrests by 6 p.m. An AFP tally cited by French media counted at least 31 people seriously injured by security forces since the protests began; authorities have issued no official injury total.

Youth- and worker-led rallies also took place in Portugal and Spain. French unions have called another public-sector strike and demonstrations for Dec. 1, demanding higher public-sector pay and renewed wage negotiations.

title: Farmers turn to soil and water strategies as climate extremes intensify
description:
Farmers and researchers are testing soil, irrigation and crop-management measures as drought, flooding and extreme heat strain agriculture in Poland, Sweden and Senegal. At a Polish agriculture conference, experts said drought resilience depends on assessing soil conditions and improving long-term water retention. A Swedish research project is assessing a system designed to store water in dry periods and release it during floods.

In Senegal, farmers and agricultural workers report hotter planting seasons and fewer hours in the fields, while shared irrigation along the Senegal River has become vital. The Swedish project will test the system under different climate scenarios and develop implementation guidance. Researchers say its effects on soil ecosystems and nutrient releases still need study.

Field trade-offs: Strip-till with fertilizer placed below the surface can work well in dry conditions, but heavy machinery on wet soil can compact the top layer; no-till remains demanding and uncommon in Poland (tygodnik-rolniczy.pl). Heat and wages: Temperatures at a Senegal greenhouse have reached 111 degrees, prompting workers to leave; shorter shifts or extra breaks can cost workers bonuses that could double or triple their daily pay (washingtonpost.com).

title: A 50-year-old theory about evolution may have been wrong all along
description: A decades-old theory suggesting that evolution protects its most important genes from mutations has been dealt a major blow. An extensive new analysis of mutations in bacteria and yeast found no evidence that essential genes mutate less frequently than other genes. Researchers say earlier studies may have been misled by harmful mutations that disappeared through natural selection before scientists could detect them.

title: Michigan court leaves state renewable energy siting rules largely intact
description:
The Michigan Supreme Court declined to hear a challenge by dozens of townships to Public Act 233, the 2023 law that lets the state approve certain renewable energy projects when local zoning rules exceed the law’s standards. The order leaves most of that framework in place, but the court also ruled that any local government affected by a project—not only the government with zoning authority—can qualify as an affected local unit.

The justices have not resolved a separate dispute over when a 30-day deadline begins for local officials to tell developers they have a qualifying ordinance. They scheduled arguments for the January 2027 session and directed the parties to file briefs in December and January. The order does not approve or reject any specific energy project.

title: Ebola death toll in Congo exceeds 5,700 as response lags
description:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 11,700 confirmed cases and 5,700 deaths as of Nov. 19, making it the country’s largest and deadliest. Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. The Bundibugyo strain is driving the outbreak, and no approved vaccine or targeted treatment is available for it. Health workers say early cases can be difficult to identify because initial symptoms resemble those of other illnesses.

Late detection, population movement and mistrust of response teams have hindered containment, while attacks on health workers and burial teams have further complicated the response. On Nov. 17, health workers in Butembo, North Kivu, escalated a month-long strike over unpaid wages and bonuses, halting even minimum service at treatment centers.

title: Projectiles hit two tankers near Hormuz as shipping traffic falls
description:
Unidentified projectiles struck two tankers sailing out of the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, Nov. 21, near Oman’s Khasab, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), a British maritime security agency, said. One tanker was hit on the stern about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab; the second was struck in its engine room about 17 nautical miles east. UKMTO reported no casualties and said the incidents might involve the same vessel. The environmental impact was unknown.

Iran’s army said a tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in a restricted area east of the strait. It alleged that the vessel had switched off its identification and navigation systems. Reuters could not verify that account or establish whether it referred to either UKMTO incident. The U.S. military has said it cleared mines from the main shipping routes.

The attacks occurred during the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, which began on Feb. 28. Iran has restricted passage through the waterway, while Washington has blockaded Iranian ports and escorted tankers. Before the war, nearly one-fifth of global crude oil supplies passed through the strait. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said a Qatari delegation held two hours of talks in Tehran on Friday. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran’s demands must be met before discussing the strait’s reopening.

title: Former Italian police chief dies as inquiry into Borsellino case continues
description:
Gianni De Gennaro, Italy’s former national police chief, was found dead at his country home in Tuscany on Saturday, Nov. 21, while under investigation over alleged efforts to obstruct inquiries into the 1992 killing of anti-mafia magistrate Paolo Borsellino. Italian media reported an apparent suicide. Authorities opened a separate inquiry into the circumstances of his death, and an autopsy was pending.

Prosecutors in Caltanissetta, Sicily, had sought house arrest for De Gennaro, alleging he helped obstruct efforts to establish what happened after the car-bomb attack that killed Borsellino and five police officers in Palermo. A judge rejected the request, but prosecutors appealed. De Gennaro denied wrongdoing, and no court had ruled on the allegations.

The investigation continues to examine unanswered questions about the bombing inquiry, including the disappearance of Borsellino’s red notebook. De Gennaro had been due to testify next month, and a hearing on the house-arrest appeal was scheduled for Dec. 1. After his death, Borsellino’s son said another piece of the truth might have gone with him.

title: Scientists say the human family tree may need a radical rewrite
description: The human family tree may need a major overhaul. New research from Monash University challenges the traditional classification of our ancient ancestors, arguing that species such as Australopithecus and Paranthropus should be grouped within our own genus, Homo. As scientists uncover more fossils and analyze evolutionary relationships, the boundaries that once separated these ancient relatives are becoming increasingly difficult to defend.

title: EU-Indonesia pact targets battery materials and barriers to European exports
description:
The European Union and Indonesia signed a trade and investment pact in Brussels on Nov. 21 to improve European access to nickel and cobalt and remove Indonesian tariffs of up to 50% on imported EU cars. The agreements include rules intended to make raw-material supply chains more predictable, including a ban on export monopolies and safeguards against discriminatory pricing.

Indonesia’s import duty on EU vehicles is due to be phased out over five years. The pact also cuts tariffs on most European agricultural exports, currently worth about €1 billion a year, but excludes rice, sugar, eggs, fresh bananas and ethanol from the tariff cuts. It protects 221 European geographical indications, names linking products to their regions of origin.

The deal follows negotiations launched in 2016 and concluded in September 2025. It now needs European Parliament consent and Indonesia’s domestic ratification before provisional application, expected in early 2027. The EU’s existing preferential trade scheme for Indonesian goods is due to end on Jan. 1, 2027.

title: Algeria advances $3.5 billion desert dairy complex for 270,000 cows
description:
A $3.5 billion dairy and crop complex under construction in Algeria’s Adrar province is designed to combine feed production, a herd of 270,000 dairy cows and milk powder processing across about 117,000 hectares. Its planned output of up to 100,000 metric tons of milk powder a year could cover about half of Algeria’s demand for the product, with the aim of reducing imports.

Temperatures in the region exceed 40°C for more than 130 days a year, and the project’s irrigation and cooling systems require continuous power and water supplies. Initial fodder crops are already growing, and barley was harvested in May. Production is scheduled to start in late 2027.

title: 11 career decisions high performers regret making too late
description:
Some career decisions become costly only after too much time has passed. The following insights, from experts in the field, reveal which moves high performers often wish they had made sooner, from protecting their health to asking for help and building stronger networks. These lessons offer clear steps for making better choices before regret sets in.

Delegate Authority While Capacity Remains

The single decision high performers almost always make too late is firing themselves from day-to-day fulfillment, because their ego is still addicted to being the hero inside the company.

When I founded my first Scandinavian fine jewelry brand in Oslo at 22, I built our early momentum by personally touching every single bottleneck: approving every creative cut, negotiating every creator seeding deal, and rewriting campaign copy at 2:00 a.m. Because revenue was climbing and we were landing cultural placements like Khaby Lame and Vogue Scandinavia, I mistook exhaustion for leverage.

The turning point came when I realized that by being the best operator in the room, I had capped the company’s valuation at the limit of my personal nervous system. High performers wait until they hit burnout to build standard operating procedures and delegate authority, whereas you actually have to hand off the keys while you still have 40% left in the tank.

Once I forced myself to step out of daily order orchestration and document our visual and distribution protocols so the business ran without my fingerprints on every transaction, two things happened: Our enterprise value became transferable (allowing us to close a clean private acquisition exit in Q4 2024), and my own bandwidth opened up to direct film productions. If I could go back, I would have documented and delegated my favorite tasks 12 months earlier, not just the chores I hated.

Mommi Live, founder, managing partner & creative director, Mommi Limited

Archive Evidence Beyond External Platforms

Keeping their track record inside someone else’s platform.

High performers usually build their reputation where the work happens: an employer’s system, a marketplace profile, a client’s internal tools. It feels like the record will always be there. Then the job ends, the platform changes its rules, or the old proof simply stops being shown, and years of results are hard to point to.

I learned this with my own business. I started selling video editing on Fiverr in 2020, while I was studying computer science. That grew into Mark Studios, which has completed more than 8,000 orders and earned 4,500+ reviews, with a 4.9 rating and Top Rated status. But Fiverr only shows roughly the last two years of reviews, so the visible proof of the early years keeps shrinking even as the total grows. The work was real. The evidence just lived somewhere I didn’t control.

What I’d do differently, and what I tell anyone doing great work inside a company or a platform: Keep your own record from day one. Write a short case study after every project that matters, with the problem, what you did, and a measurable result. For a channel whose thumbnails and titles we’ve handled since August 2025, VidIQ showed views up 30.1% week over week when we captured the stats in May. That number now sits in a case study on my own website instead of only in a client conversation. Ask for testimonials you’re allowed to reuse, and save the numbers while they’re fresh.

Your reputation is an asset. Make sure you hold a copy of it.

Mark Santos, founder & creative director, Mark Studios LLC

Ask for Help Before Depletion

The decision I see high performers regret most isn’t burning out. It’s waiting until they’re depleted to ask for help, because by then the choice is already gone. Their body makes it for them.

I’m a licensed counselor supervisor and president of a South Carolina practice with more than 60 therapists across 10 offices, plus online therapy. I watch this play out in my own field constantly. The strongest clinicians I supervise are usually the last ones to bring a hard case to supervision. Asking feels like admitting they can’t handle it, and they’ve built their whole identity around being the person others lean on. So they carry it quietly. And it doesn’t show up right away. It shows up months later as irritability, or dread on Sunday nights, or a sudden wish to quit work they used to love.

What I tell them is pretty straightforward. Build the support in while things are still going well. Put a standing check-in on the calendar with a supervisor, a mentor, or a therapist before there’s anything urgent to report. When I started my practice with my husband, David, in 2019, I learned fast that the same logic applies to running a company. Support that you set up early costs you maybe an hour a week. Support that you set up late costs you a year of recovery. The best time to ask for help is when you don’t feel like you need it yet.

Kenza Haddock, president, Oceanic Counseling Group

Broadcast Accomplishments to Gain Advocacy

High performers are great at getting things done, often to the detriment of their career progression. If you’re so busy taking care of things, then communicating out what you’re accomplishing is often the last thing on your list. That’s either because you don’t want to brag, or you assume others know what you’re working on. Not learning to communicate up and out is often a regret. 

I’ve worked with a senior leader whose manager was let go. They established relationships with their new manager and also with other senior leaders in the organization. They learned to communicate regularly as a part of their role to inform the what and the why of their accomplishments through one reorg after another. When yet another manager was let go, they were promoted into the role due to the awareness and extended support they’d built. 

I’m now working with a younger employee with a new manager on how to own their weekly reporting, proactively communicating to the team what their weekly accomplishments are and how these fit into the greater goals. People can only advocate for you if they can say what you actually do. High performers often learn this alternate side of their role far too late.

Dana Zellers, executive & leadership coach, team facilitator, Dana Zellers

Own Your Professional Future

I’ve talked with more than a thousand executives in the past four years and the biggest regrets that I hear from high performers is relying on their employers to take care of them instead of taking ownership for their career decisions.

I have had more clients than I can count who worked for Fortune 100 employers for 20+ years. They believed that they would retire with that company, but then the business changed, they lost their job, and they were left trying to figure out where to go next.

No matter where you are in your career, you need to remember that companies are usually going to look out for themselves first. You need to plan your career accordingly. “Job hugging” has been the newest trend, where workers hang on to jobs that they don’t necessarily love. Sure, there is risk in leaving your job, but there is also risk at staying in your current job, especially if layoffs are on the horizon.

Staying open to potential opportunities, both actively through networking and passively through an optimized LinkedIn profile, is key to building a career that lasts.

Colleen Paulson, executive career consultant, Ageless Careers

Align Ambition With Desired Work

One decision high performers often make too late is to actively manage their careers rather than assuming that success in their current jobs will take care of that for them. Excelling at your job and managing your career are related, but they’re not the same thing. I’ve seen this play out in two ways.

First, high performers become exceptionally good at identifying what it takes to succeed within their organizations. They earn promotions, navigate politics, and build expertise and relationships. But they don’t always stop to ask whether what they’re building is what they actually want.

Over the last few years, I’ve worked with leaders who realized that the roles they’d spent years working toward had taken them further away from the work they loved, whether that’s working directly with clients or coaching their teams. We often think about the title and impact, but not the altitude we’ll have to lead at. A promotion often means moving away from doing the work yourself to creating the conditions for others to do it, through strategy, resource allocation, and management. That’s a very different job.

Second, high performers forget to build career optionality before they need it. They invest heavily in building skills, relationships, and credibility within their organizations. That’s important, but incomplete. Internal recognition matters, but so does building an external professional network. Think of it as a savings account you’re contributing to over time.

Too often, I’ve coached leaders who gave everything to their organizations, sometimes staying for more than a decade, only to find themselves facing a layoff, burnout, or a desire to pivot—and realizing they had limited external networks and little understanding of how their skills would translate elsewhere.

A few simple ways to avoid these traps:

• Before pursuing a promotion, talk to people already in the role. Understand what their day-to-day looks like, what they’ve had to give up, and what success actually requires.

• While you’re happily employed, invest in relationships outside your organization and learn about other industries. Volunteer opportunities and nonprofit board service can be excellent ways to do this while also giving back.

• The goal is not to constantly be on a job hunt. It’s to make sure you’re building a career that reflects what you want, with the flexibility to make different choices along the way.

Lisa Friscia, president and founder, Franca Consulting

Pursue Ventures Through Small Bets

One decision high performers often regret making too late is waiting to act on an entrepreneurial idea because it feels safer to stay on secure footing. With more responsibility, high performers can get attached to income or get sucked into “golden handcuffs.” They’re less likely to leave for a more enjoyable job or take a risk at starting something up. I have seen this with seasoned corporate leaders who had a viable concept for years, but once they were settled with a mortgage, family responsibilities, and a stable role, the leap started to feel like too much to lose. 

The regret often sharpens when they later watch someone else succeed with a similar idea, because possibility suddenly looks like proof that they could have moved earlier. What could have been done differently is keeping the risk muscle active through small, regular bets while still employed, such as testing the idea in low-stakes ways and building comfort with uncertainty. That approach reduces the gap between the idea and bringing it to market, so the decision is not one big, intimidating jump. 

Also, it’s important to have accountability partners who ask us hard questions or challenge the status quo related to our experience, comfort, and career. How much money is enough? When is the right time? I hear high performers regret missed opportunities with a radical role departure or a job abroad or starting something new, going back to school when they were younger. We feel guilted or bullied into the norm by our families, peers, neighbors and society to do the “right” and “responsible” thing, then later wish we had taken the road less traveled or taken a risk.

Janice Perkins, executive coach, Janice Perkins

Restore Health Through Daily Habits

The one decision high performers often regret is not focusing on their health and well-being as a function of improving their daily performance. 

All too often, high performers have had success all of their lives. They create habits in their 20s when their energy levels are high and their body can bounce back relatively quickly. As they start to advance their career in their 30s, 40s, and 50s, these high performers continue with these same habits, focusing only on work. Working late, missing sleep, skipping meals, and perhaps drinking alcohol (even in moderate amounts) drain more and more energy, physical and mental, from their daily output. 

To these habits, they add coffee to wake up and sugar intake to combat the energy crashes. This leads to poor sleep, and the cycle continues every day. 

It is possible to reverse these bad habits with small intentional changes in one’s daily lifestyle. A couple of simple examples are arising at the same time every day, including weekends, and getting morning daylight within the first 60-120 minutes of waking up.

Steve Fiore, executive performance advisor, Rooted in Curiosity

Serve Your Network Regularly

As a career coach, I usually connect with high performers when they are in the midst of, or planning for, a transition. The #1 regret I hear is that leaders feel they lost touch with their network while building their careers.

They understandably hesitate to make an ask when they haven’t connected in three, five, or even 10+ years. It can feel cringey and awkward reaching out when so much time has passed.

But now more than ever, your network is your career net worth. So I hope more high achievers keep that in mind.

The easiest way to keep in touch with your network? Be a helper.

Haley McNeel Drake, résumé writer & career coach, The Career Revisory

Exit Places That Diminish Your Worth

One important decision I’ve seen time and time again among high performers is not leaving an organization sooner when their value went unrecognized. Being a high performer doesn’t automatically translate to timely promotions or special accolades for great work. 

In the pursuit of success, a high performer can work to increase their visibility and yet those efforts don’t lead to a promotion. Not because they’re doing anything wrong or focused on things that won’t get them noticed, but because of office politics or favoritism. What people often overlook and hate to admit is that you simply may be in the wrong environment where no matter what you do, your value will be unrecognized. 

For high performers, staying too long in an environment after making efforts to be “promotion ready” will eventually catch up, once they end up in an environment where they are valued, appreciated, and recognized for their work.

Owning your competence, knowing your value, and being honest with yourself is part of high performance. Not getting a promotion the first time you ask for one isn’t necessarily a sign that you need to start looking or you’re being undervalued. However, the challenge arises when the same cycle repeats, and you’re getting empty promises instead of a kept word. 

Pay attention to nuance, yes: changes in the broader organization, natural attrition, etc. Timing is everything. But also, give yourself a timeline. If the opportunities you want to pursue don’t become available within that timeline, and those in charge can’t give you a blueprint to help you get where you want to be, you then make a different decision. And that could be planning your exit.

Lisa De Nicola, leadership & executive coach; founder, HER Lead; Lisa De Nicola

Broaden Expertise Outside Familiar Functions

One decision high performers often make too late is stepping outside the area where they’ve already proven themselves.

When you’re good at something, you tend to get more of it. You get promoted, take on bigger responsibilities, and become the person everyone relies on. That’s great for your career, but it can also keep you in a fairly narrow lane.

Earlier in my career at HD Supply, I spent time working directly with branch managers, and one thing I did was lead financial literacy sessions. These were for people making decisions every day about pricing, inventory, customers, and how to run their businesses.

I learned a tremendous amount from those conversations. They helped me understand the operating decisions behind the financial results, and that made me a much better finance leader.

Looking back, I would have sought out more of that exposure earlier rather than waiting for opportunities to come through my formal responsibilities.

My advice to high performers is to take on something outside your comfort zone before you feel completely ready. Spend time with customers, get involved in operations, or volunteer for a project that forces you to learn another part of the business.

Being really good at your current job gets you noticed. Understanding how the whole business works prepares you for the next one.

Thomas DeFabrizio, CFO, Vertage

title: Signal warns AI agents can expose other participants’ encrypted chats
description:
Messaging app Signal says operating-system AI assistants and third-party agents can expose private chats beyond its control, putting all participants’ privacy at risk. Signal’s mobile screenshot restrictions aim to block one route, but the company says they do not stop agents from reading locally stored data or using other system-level access.

Meta’s Muse agent reportedly accessed Signal messages through Android notification permissions and used accessibility and screenshot tools on a Mac; Apple later closed that specific Mac pathway with a system update. Meta said Muse accesses other apps only through permissions users explicitly grant. Signal is asking Apple, Google and Microsoft to let apps opt out of screen reading, notification access and file access, and to provide clearer technical documentation.

title: AI-driven sell-off erases most 2026 gains as S&P 500 falls 11.6%
description:
